1	# Guitar Hero Bot — System Specification
2	
3	> Top-level overview. For implementation detail of any single subproject, follow the pointers in §3. Each subproject owns its own spec; this document does not duplicate them.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## 1. Mission
8	
9	Build an autonomous robot that plays Guitar Hero / Rock Band on a real Wii guitar controller by watching the game video, detecting notes in real time, and pressing physical buttons in sync with the music. The system must run end-to-end without a host PC in the runtime path, produce reference-quality detector output that lighter detectors can be trained against, and provide an on-device operator UI for calibration, mode control, and replay.
10	
11	## 2. Current architecture
12	
13	Three pieces, one runtime brain:
14	
15	```
16	Wii ──HDMI──► ElectronWarp ──HDMI──► TC358743 ──CSI-2──┐
17	                                                       ▼
18	   ┌──────────────────────  marvin (SAM9X75)  ────────────┐
19	   │  HDMI capture → CV detect → timing pipeline → cmds   │
20	   │           ↑              detector-state bus          │
21	   │           │                       ▲                  │
22	   │           │  10.1″ LVDS + maxtouch │                  │
23	   │           │       (operator UI)    │                  │
24	   │           └────────── SD card ─────┘  (recording)    │
25	   └────────┬──────────────────────────┬───────────────────┘
26	            │ USB CDC host (cmds)      │ USB CDC host (ADC)
27	            ▼                          │
28	   ┌──────────────────────────────────┐│
29	   │   fretboard (PIC32CM6408)        │┘
30	   │   ADC scan ↔ open-drain GPIO     │
31	   └────────┬─────────────────────────┘
32	            │ GPIO
33	            ▼
34	   Wii guitar controller ──► Wii (closes the loop)
35	
36	                ◇ off-band: dev PC running fret-tuner
37	                  (calibration / detector tuning / replay)
38	```
39	
40	**Per-tier role summary:**
41	
42	- **marvin** — SAM9X75 Curiosity host. Owns HDMI capture, the *reference* CV note detector, ingest of fretboard ADC samples, the chord/strum timing pipeline, command emission to fretboard, the on-device LVDS+touch operator UI, and reference-data recording to SD. The runtime brain.
43	- **fretboard** — PIC32CM6408PL10048 MCU on a sensor/actuator board. Streams 5-channel phototransistor ADC up to marvin and converts incoming bitmask commands into open-drain GPIO presses on a Wii guitar controller. Has a standalone fallback mode where it runs its own chord FIFO without marvin in the loop.
44	- **fret-tuner** — Off-band Python tool (FastAPI + browser UI, Linux/macOS PC). Used at the bench for sensor calibration, detector-algorithm tuning, and replay analysis of recordings produced by marvin. Not in the runtime path.

94	The actuator choice is intentionally still open — `hardware/actuators/` contains design + test-protocol docs for three candidates.
95	
96	## 6. Cross-cutting decisions
97	
98	- **Architecture pivot.** The original PC-hosted / Elgato-USB-capture / PS2 / single-PIC-actuator design is retired. Source documents are preserved at [`docs/archive/`](docs/archive/) for design-rationale reference; they are *not* maintained.
99	- **`frame_epoch` is the master sync token.** A 32-bit counter incremented by marvin's video task on every captured ISC frame. Every detector-state record, emitted command, and recording artifact — including data from off-board observers — keys off this token so multi-source data can be aligned post-hoc. Detail in [marvin spec §4.6](firmware/marvin/docs/spec.md).
100	- **Reference data persists on marvin's SD card.** Detector-state + sparse raw BGR888 keyframes (default 1 keyframe/sec) + raw ADC stream + emitted commands. Off-board detectors record their own data keyed by `frame_epoch` and align offline.
101	- **Centralized timing on marvin, with a fretboard-takeover fallback.** marvin runs the chord-window FIFO and strum scheduler by default; an operator-mode toggle hands timing back to fretboard's standalone `fret_button.c` while marvin still records observations.
102	- **Operating modes are independent toggles**, not a global state machine: `detect_enable`, `marvin_timing_enable`, `actuate_enable`, `record_enable`. Named modes (idle / calibrate / dry-run / play / replay / record) are presets over them.
103

109	| ✅ | marvin DDR → 10.1″ LVDS panel display (HEO, per-frame swap, pillarboxed/letterboxed) |

113	| ✅ | marvin perf-log USB CDC export — live RTOS analytics + pixel strip viewer (`tools/marvin-perf`) |

115	| ✅ | **M2** — fretboard ↔ marvin link (USB CDC host over EDBG; commands flowing) |
116	| ✅ | **M3** — end-to-end play (timing pipeline + fretboard actuation; Expert and Easy tested) |
117	| 🚧 | **M4** — recording-to-SD (detector-state + keyframes + ADC + commands) |
118	| 🚧 | **M5** — operator UI v0; manual-control surface (8 buttons) done; full live-view + mode-toggle UI not started |
119	| 🚧 | **M6**+ — calibration UI, replay, fretboard-takeover validation, game-state controller |
120	
121	Detail (definitions of done, demos) in [marvin spec §8](firmware/marvin/docs/spec.md).
122	
123	## 8. What this is *not*
124	
125	To anchor against the original architecture (preserved in `docs/archive/`):
126	
127	- **Not PC-hosted.** marvin is the runtime brain; no host PC is required for play.
128	- **Not USB-capture / Elgato.** Video is captured directly off HDMI via a TC358743 → MIPI CSI-2 path into the SAM9X75's ISC.
129	- **Not PS2.** The supported console is the Nintendo Wii (with an ElectronWarp component → HDMI converter).
130	- **Not a single-MCU actuator.** Sensing and timing live on marvin; fretboard is a sensor/actuator MCU, not a solo controller (with the explicit exception of the standalone-fallback mode).
131	- **Not OpenCV / Python at runtime.** CV runs natively on the SAM9X75 (Cortex-A5). Python (`fret-tuner`) is a bench tool only.

1	# edge-ai — Design Specification
2	
3	> **Status:** design in progress. No code yet. Phases 1–4 are offline Python on a dev PC; phase 5 is the first hardware touch. See [rollout.md](rollout.md) for phase definitions and [review.md](review.md) for open questions, risks, and rejected alternatives.
4	
5	## 1. Purpose & scope
6	
7	A development effort to build a small ML model that takes the fretboard's 5-channel phototransistor ADC stream and emits the same 1-byte fret + strum bitmask that marvin's timing pipeline produces today. Once trained, validated, and deployed, it removes marvin from the runtime gameplay loop.
8	
9	This is intentionally an **offline-first development effort**. Almost all of the work — capture, label, train, validate, debug — happens on a dev PC against recorded marvin self-play data. The on-device deployment is the *last* phase, after the model has been proven offline.
10	
11	**In scope:**
12	
13	- Training-data plumbing: a new export mode in [tools/marvin-perf](../../marvin-perf/) that turns marvin self-play perf-log captures into labelled CSV.
14	- Host-side training, validation, and model artifacts.
15	- Eventual on-device runtime integration. Today's intended target is the fretboard MCU (PIC32CM6408PL10048, M0+ @ 24 MHz) — see [runtime.md](runtime.md) — but the offline phases are MCU-agnostic and the target can be revisited if the model size/shape demands it.
16	
17	**Out of scope:**
18	
19	- Replacing marvin as the *reference* detector. Marvin remains the source of truth for training and diagnostics.
20	- Game-state / menu navigation. The edge AI plays gameplay only; whole-session control still belongs to marvin (system [SPEC.md §4.8 of marvin spec](../../../firmware/marvin/docs/spec.md)).
21	- The fretboard-takeover fallback ([fretboard journal](../../../firmware/fretboard/docs/journal.md), 2026-06-02 entry). That mode runs `fret_button.c` standalone; the edge AI is a separate operating mode if/when it deploys to fretboard.
22	
23	## 2. Why now
24	
25	Two concrete pressures came out of the recent training-data work:
26	
27	### 2.1 Spatial mismatch between current label and ADC
28	
29	The current SensiML CSV exporter ([tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/exporters/sensiml_csv.py](../../marvin-perf/marvin_perf/exporters/sensiml_csv.py)) labels each fretboard ADC sample with `cv_marvin_v1`'s `pressed_mask`, broadcast forward by `frame_epoch`. But the two sensors look at different points on the screen:
30	
31	- `cv_marvin_v1` samples at `y = 311` ([detector/cv_marvin_v1.c](../../../firmware/marvin/default/src/detector/cv_marvin_v1.c)), above the strike line.
32	- The five phototransistors physically sit "above the TV strike line" ([fretboard SPEC.md](../../../firmware/fretboard/SPEC.md)), at a different (unverified) row than `y = 311`.
33	
34	Same falling note, different sensors, different times. Aligning them on `frame_epoch` bakes in a fixed offset that is only correct at one scroll speed. Fixing this in hardware is finicky and locks the system to a single mechanical layout.
35	
36	### 2.2 Strum timing missing from the AI's job
37	
38	Today's training pipeline emits per-fret pressed labels only. The chord window + +220 ms strum scheduler ([actuator/timing_pipeline.c:21,198,199](../../../firmware/marvin/default/src/actuator/timing_pipeline.c)) is real, non-trivial work that the AI is not being asked to learn. Whatever the AI replaces, the timing pipeline still has to live somewhere.
39	
40	The simplifying observation is that the model only needs to learn *when* to strum — not *which direction* — because alternating up/down is a human ergonomics constraint the controller doesn't enforce. That collapses 2 strum bits into 1 and halves the rare-class label density problem.
41	
42	## 3. Decisions locked
43	
44	| Decision | Why (one line) |
45	|---|---|
46	| **Output:** 6 bits — 5 fret bits + 1 collapsed strum bit. At the wire it's emitted as strum-down (bit 5) only; bit 6 is always 0. | Pulls strum timing into the AI; alternating up/down is a human ergonomic constraint the controller doesn't enforce. The collapse happens *at export time*, not in the recording — `PERF_REC_ACTUATOR` keeps both strum bits as captured so a future human-trainer corpus can preserve direction information for other uses. |
47	| **Supervision:** distillation against `PERF_REC_ACTUATOR.intended_mask` from marvin self-play. | Sidesteps spatial mismatch — labels are marvin's chosen byte, not a CV intermediate. |
48	| **Intended deployment target:** fretboard PIC32CM6408PL10048, M0+ @ 24 MHz. | Removes marvin from the gameplay loop; truly "edge". Offline phases are MCU-agnostic, so this can be revisited if the model demands more compute. |
49	| **Inputs at inference (v1):** the existing 5 ADC channels only. | Cheapest start; per-fret HW expansion deferred (see [review.md](review.md) Q1). |
50	| **Training corpus:** marvin self-play recordings only. | Simplest closure. AI inherits marvin's behavior — good and bad — see [review.md §risks](review.md#risks). |
51	
52	The key insight that makes this work: **distilling against marvin's commands dissolves the spatial-mismatch problem.** The label is the byte marvin chose with the +220 ms strum delay already baked in. The model just needs a wide enough causal window of ADC to learn whatever delay maps photo dip → strum, regardless of where the photoxistors physically sit. Mechanical alignment becomes a non-requirement.
53	
54	## 4. Document map
55	
56	| Doc | What's in it |
57	|---|---|
58	| [architecture.md](architecture.md) | Training-time and inference-time data flow; cadence; sanity-check that the shape addresses §2 |
59	| [training.md](training.md) | Exporter changes, CSV schema, capture protocol, model architecture |
60	| [runtime.md](runtime.md) | Eventual on-device deployment integration — module shape, callback wiring, mode toggle |
61	| [rollout.md](rollout.md) | Phased plan with explicit offline/hardware split, plus per-phase verification |
62	| [review.md](review.md) | Risks, open questions surfaced for reviewer pushback, and alternatives considered |
63
```

1	# training
2	
3	The offline pipeline: how marvin self-play recordings become training data, and the model that consumes them.
4	
5	## 1. Data flow
6	
7	Recap (full diagram in [architecture.md](architecture.md)):
8	
9	```
10	perf-log capture (.bin)
11	    │  contains: SESSION + DETECTOR + ACTUATOR + FRETBOARD_RAW
12	    │
13	    ▼
14	marvin-perf  export-ml --labels=actuator capture.bin out.csv
15	    │
16	    ▼
17	SensiML CSV (per-row: 5 ADC + 6 labels)
18	    │
19	    ▼
20	host training (PyTorch / MPLAB ML)
21	```
22	
23	## 2. New label source in the SensiML exporter
24	
25	Modify [tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/exporters/sensiml_csv.py](../../marvin-perf/marvin_perf/exporters/sensiml_csv.py) to add an `--labels=actuator` mode (the current `pressed_mask` path stays as `--labels=detector` for back-compat):
26	
27	- Track the most recent `Actuator` record alongside `last_detector` (decoder already exists at [tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/records.py:300](../../marvin-perf/marvin_perf/records.py)).
28	- Forward-fill `Actuator.intended_mask` onto each `FretboardRaw` row, emitting frets at bits 0..4 verbatim and a **collapsed strum bit** = `((intended_mask >> 5) | (intended_mask >> 6)) & 1` (logical OR of strum-down and strum-up).
29	- Emit a per-export stat `n_strum_events` so we can verify strum-bit density on a captured corpus.
30	
31	The collapse is a property of *this* exporter mode, not the raw capture. `PERF_REC_ACTUATOR` records both strum bits as marvin emitted them; a future training corpus that includes human-trainer data (where alternating up/down is meaningful as ergonomic ground truth) keeps both bits intact on disk and can either be exported through the same collapse for this model, or through a future direction-aware exporter for a different model variant.
32	
33	## 3. CSV schema
34	
35	```
36	timestamp,
37	ph_green, ph_red, ph_yellow, ph_blue, ph_orange,
38	fret_green, fret_red, fret_yellow, fret_blue, fret_orange,
39	strum
40	```
41	
42	Same row cadence as today (one row per `FretboardRaw` ≈ 240 Hz).
43	
44	## 4. Capture protocol
45	
46	A training corpus is a set of marvin self-play perf-log captures across difficulty levels (Easy, Medium, Expert) and song variety. Each capture must have all of `SESSION + DETECTOR + ACTUATOR + FRETBOARD_RAW` enabled in the `PERF_CMD_SET_TYPE_MASK`.
47	
48	A held-out song is reserved per session for offline validation; the same held-out set should be reused across training iterations so per-iteration metrics are comparable.
49	
50	## 5. Model
51	
52	### 5.1 Recommended baseline
53	
54	- **Input:** 5 ADC channels × 60 samples (250 ms causal window) @ 240 Hz, int16 → int8 after normalisation.
55	- **Output:** 6 sigmoids during training (independent BCE per bit) — 5 frets + 1 collapsed strum; thresholded to binary at deploy. The runtime stage maps the strum bit into the wire byte's bit 5 (strum-down); bit 6 stays 0.
56	- **Architecture:** MPLAB ML / SensiML auto-pipeline first — windowed feature extractor (MAV, std, slope, peak, simple FIR taps) feeding a gradient-boosted ensemble or tiny dense head. SensiML targets exactly this MCU class.
57	- **Fallback if auto-pipeline misses strum timing:** tiny causal 1D-CNN, two conv layers ~8 channels, kernel 5–7, dilation `[1, 4]`. Quantise to int8.
58	
59	### 5.2 Why 250 ms
60	
61	`TP_STRUM_DELAY_MS = 220` ([timing_pipeline.c:21](../../../firmware/marvin/default/src/actuator/timing_pipeline.c)). 60 samples × 4.17 ms = 250 ms gives ≈30 ms margin around the photo-dip-to-strum-bit relationship. Window length is the most important hyperparameter to sweep — see [review.md Q3](review.md#q3-look-ahead-vs-now-cast).
62	
63	### 5.3 Quantisation
64	
65	int8 weights, int16 activations during the conv layers, int8 at the output. The intended deployment target has no FPU; floating-point inference is a non-starter. If the offline phase chooses to revisit the deployment target, the quantisation choice may relax.
66	
67	## 6. Loss
68	
69	Independent BCE per output bit, weighted to compensate for class imbalance:
70	
71	- Fret bits are dense (often 1 for many ticks per chord); near-1:1 weighting works.
72	- The strum bit is sparse (≤2 ticks per chord, ~5% of samples); weight strongly to avoid the trivial "always 0" minimum. Focal loss is a sane alternative if simple weighting plateaus.
73	
74	If per-bit independence produces poor strum timing, switch to a multi-class head over common chord shapes — see [review.md §alternatives](review.md#12-alternatives-considered).
75
```

1	# architecture
2	
3	How the edge AI fits at training time and at inference time. For decisions and the document map, see [SPEC.md](SPEC.md).
4	
5	## 1. Training-time data flow (offline)
6	
7	```
8	Wii ──► marvin (cv_marvin_v1 + timing_pipeline)
9	          │   │
10	          │   ├── PERF_REC_ACTUATOR (intended_mask, strum_dir)   ──┐
11	          │   └── (commands over USB CDC to fretboard)              │
12	          │                                                          ▼
13	          │                                                  marvin-perf
14	          │                                                   (offline)
15	          │   ▲                                                      │
16	          │   │ PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW (5×ADC @ 240 Hz)              │
17	          │   │                                                      │
18	          │   └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────►│
19	          │                                                          │
20	          │                                                          ▼
21	          │                                                   SensiML CSV
22	          │                                            (per-row: 5 ADC + 6 labels)
23	                                                                     │
24	                                                                     ▼
25	                                                        host training (PyTorch /
26	                                                              MPLAB ML)
27	                                                                     │
28	                                                                     ▼
29	                                                            quantised model
30	                                                              (int8 / int16)
31	```
32	
33	Both record streams already flow through perf-log keyed by `frame_epoch` + `ts_counter`. The exporter joins them offline. See [training.md](training.md) for the exporter change and CSV schema.
34	
35	## 2. Inference-time data flow (eventual on-device)
36	
37	```
38	fretboard TC0 callback @ 240 Hz:
39	    fret_scan_all()             ──► s_adc_ring[60][5]    (250 ms history)
40	                                       │
41	                                       ▼
42	                                 model_infer(ring) ──► uint8_t cmd_byte
43	                                       │
44	                                       ▼
45	                                 button_apply(cmd_byte)  (open-drain GPIOs)
46	```
47	
48	`cmd_receive_update()` is bypassed when fretboard is in model-driven mode; the model owns the wire instead of marvin. See [runtime.md](runtime.md) for the integration shape.
49	
50	## 3. Inference cadence
51	
52	One inference per 240 Hz tick (every 4.17 ms), called inline from the existing TC0 callback after `fret_scan_all` and before `button_apply`. Budget per inference at 24 MHz with no FPU is ≈100 k cycles — comfortable for a model with ≲1 k MACs at int8. If host-side training reveals the chosen architecture exceeds this budget, the deployment target gets revisited (see [SPEC.md §3](SPEC.md#3-decisions-locked)) before phase 5 commits.
53	
54	## 4. Why this shape addresses both concerns
55	
56	- **Spatial mismatch dissolved.** No CV-row → photo-row alignment needed at training time. The 250 ms causal window captures whatever upstream photoxistor signal preceded the strum, regardless of physical sensor placement on the screen.
57	- **Strum timing learned.** The strum bit is part of the output. Weighted BCE (the strum bit is sparse — see [review.md §risks](review.md#risks)) lets the model learn the +220 ms photo-to-strum delay implicitly from the data.
58	- **Edge AI is end-to-end standalone.** Once deployed, fretboard runs the model on its own ADC stream; marvin can be off and gameplay still works. Marvin's role becomes "training-data source + reference detector for diagnostics + game-state controller".
59
```
</details></tool-use>

1	# rollout
2	
3	Phased plan with explicit offline / hardware split. Phases 1–4 are entirely offline (Python on a dev PC, no firmware changes). Phase 5 is the first hardware touch.
4	
5	## Offline phases
6	
7	| Phase | Goal | Done when |
8	|---|---|---|
9	| **1. Data pipeline** | Distillation labels available end-to-end | `--labels=actuator` exporter merged in [tools/marvin-perf](../../marvin-perf/); one captured-gameplay CSV inspected and shows plausible fret + strum timing |
10	| **2. Host-side baseline** | Train on PC; validate offline | MPLAB ML / PyTorch model achieves ≥95% per-bit accuracy on held-out song; strum-event timing error p95 ≤ 20 ms (one ADC sample) |
11	
12	### Phase 1 verification
13	
14	Run `marvin-perf export-ml --labels=actuator capture.bin out.csv`; manually inspect:
15	
16	- Row count ≈ 240 × duration_s.
17	- Strum bits sparse (a few %).
18	- Fret bits dense and matching gameplay difficulty.
19	
20	### Phase 2 verification
21	
22	Training script reports per-bit accuracy and strum-event timing distribution on the held-out split. Plot predicted vs. true command stream over a 30 s window; visually verify chord+strum alignment.
23	
24	## Hardware-touching phases
25	
26	| Phase | Goal | Done when |
27	|---|---|---|
28	| **3. On-device port** | Same model running on PIC32 | Inference latency < 1 ms (well inside the 4.17 ms tick); on-device output matches host inference bit-for-bit on a recorded ADC trace (within int8 quant tolerance) |
29	| **4. Side-by-side dry-run** | AI predicts but doesn't drive | New perf-log record `PERF_REC_MODEL_OUT` mirrors `Actuator` shape; recorded alongside marvin's commands; per-tick agreement tracked over a real session |
30	| **5. Cut-over** | AI drives the controller | Fretboard mode-switch flips wire ownership from `cmd_receive` to `model_infer`; gameplay scoring measured against marvin-driven baseline |
31	
32	### Phase 3 verification
33	
34	Unit test feeds a recorded ADC trace through host inference and on-device inference, asserts identical outputs (or ≤1 LSB diff after quant). On-device latency measured from a perf-log timestamp around the inference call.
35	
36	### Phase 4 verification
37	
38	Extend perf-log with `PERF_REC_MODEL_OUT` (mirrors `Actuator` shape); marvin-perf gains a side-by-side viewer; per-tick Hamming distance between model output and marvin output is logged live.
39	
40	### Phase 5 verification
41	
42	Actual game scoring on a fixed song setlist (Easy + Medium + Expert), 5+ runs each: marvin-driven baseline vs. model-driven. Pass if model-driven scores within X% of baseline (X to be set by reviewer).
43	
44	## Gating between offline and hardware phases
45	
46	A reviewer should be able to look at phase 2's metrics — per-bit accuracy, strum-event timing distribution, and a visual side-by-side over a 30 s window — and decide *yes, this is worth porting*. If the metrics are weak, [review.md](review.md) lists the natural pivots: window length sweep, multi-class chord head, two-head event detector, alternative label source. The point of the offline-first split is to take those pivots cheaply, before any on-device work has been spent.
47
```

```text
1	# review
2	
3	This is the document to push back on. Three categories: things we know can fail (risks), forks we haven't decided (open questions), and shapes we explicitly rejected (alternatives).
4	
5	## Risks
6	
7	- **Strum class imbalance.** The collapsed strum bit is 1 for ≤2 ticks per chord — well under 5% of samples. Weighted BCE / focal loss / oversampling required; verify in phase 2 that the model isn't degenerating to "always 0".
8	- **Window-too-short failure mode.** If 250 ms doesn't span the photo-dip-to-strum-bit delay across difficulty levels (Expert scrolls faster — photo dip is closer to the strum), strum-bit accuracy collapses. Sweep window in phase 2 (125 / 250 / 400 ms).
9	- **Per-bit independence vs. chord structure.** Treating bits as independent sigmoids ignores that real chords occupy a tiny subset of the 2⁶ space. If accuracy is poor, switch to a multi-class head over common chord shapes — see [§alternatives](#12-alternatives-considered).
10	- **Multi-difficulty distribution.** Train on Easy + Medium + Expert recordings; otherwise scroll-speed variation is out of distribution.
11	- **Inheriting marvin's bugs.** Distillation can't beat the teacher. Mistimed strums in marvin become mistimed strums in the AI. Acceptable for v1; future work could layer human-play recordings on top (see [Q4](#q4-strike-line-cv-detector-as-alternative-label-source)).
12	- **CDC + RTOS jitter in labels.** `PERF_REC_ACTUATOR` timestamps the moment marvin emits the command, not the moment fretboard physically asserts the GPIO. Some milliseconds of jitter from USB host scheduling and fretboard RX polling are baked into the labels. Probably fine — fretboard saw that same jitter at runtime — but worth measuring in phase 2.
13	
14	## Open questions
15	
16	> Reviewers: each of these is a real fork. Speak up *before* phase 1 lands.
17	
18	<a id="q1-hold-vs-edge-channel-per-fret"></a>
19	### Q1: Hold vs. edge channel per fret — add HW now, or wait?
20	
21	The current 5-channel ADC at 240 Hz may alias on fast transients. Two ways to add information:
22	
23	- **(a)** Two photoxistors per fret at *different* screen rows — gives the model an intrinsic "note approaching" + "note here" pair, doubling temporal resolution at hardware cost.
24	- **(b)** One extra photoxistor per fret with a colour filter, mimicking `cv_marvin_v1`'s colour-edge channel — separates "any brightness here" from "specifically a green note here".
25	
26	Either doubles the ADC scan time. Bias is to start with the existing 5 channels and only add HW if phase 2 shows the model is starved for input.
27	
28	<a id="q2-ar-feedback"></a>
29	### Q2: AR feedback — let the model see its own past output?
30	
31	Most fret-bit predictions at time `T` are highly correlated with the prediction at `T-1` (held notes). An AR model could be much smaller / more accurate. Cost: a feedback loop at runtime (bugs amplify), and harder training (teacher forcing vs. scheduled sampling). Defer until non-AR baseline is known.
32	
33	<a id="q3-look-ahead-vs-now-cast"></a>
34	### Q3: Look-ahead vs. now-cast — predict at T+K?
35	
36	Currently formulated as "predict the command at *now*". Could instead predict at `T + K_ms` to cover model+actuator latency. Irrelevant while actuators are GPIOs (latency ≈ 0); revisit when mechanical actuators land (system [SPEC.md §5](../../../SPEC.md), [hardware/actuators/](../../../hardware/actuators/)).
37	
38	<a id="q4-strike-line-cv-detector-as-alternative-label-source"></a>
39	### Q4: Strike-line CV detector as alternative label source?
40	
41	If phase 2 reveals that distillation hits a noise ceiling (CDC jitter + chord-window quantisation), an alternative is to add a `cv_strike_v1` detector on marvin that samples the *strike row* directly at 60 Hz. Cleaner labels for fret state, but loses strum-event timing — would need to re-add a rule-based "strum when strike row goes active". Flag for now, don't build.
42	
43	<a id="q5-photoxistor-placement"></a>
44	### Q5: Phototransistor placement / count — what's optimal?
45	
46	Today's PCB ([hardware/Sensor-LCD5/](../../../hardware/Sensor-LCD5/)) has 5 sensors above the strike line. Optimum-for-this-AI is unknown:
47	
48	- *Higher* on the screen → longer lookahead but more time for the note appearance to change.
49	- *At the strike line* → simplest label (the photo dip *is* the answer) but no anticipation, breaking strum scheduling.
50	- *Two rows* → see [Q1](#q1-hold-vs-edge-channel-per-fret).
51	
52	Open until phase 2 data tells us which placement makes the model's job easiest.
53	
54	## 12. Alternatives considered
55	
56	Three other shapes were on the table before the current distillation choice landed:
57	
58	- **Shape A — frame classifier with co-located CV.** Model predicts `pressed_mask` from a single ADC sample; labels come from a *new* CV detector at the photoxistor row. Pros: small model, easy to label. Rejected because it still leaves the strum decision outside the AI, and forces mechanical alignment between CV and photoxistors — exactly the problem we're trying to dissolve.
59	- **Shape B — sequence-to-strike-line oracle.** Model takes a causal ADC window, outputs what's at the strike row right now. Labels come from a new strike-row CV detector. Pros: clean physical meaning ("predict the moment of truth"). Rejected because, like A, it doesn't include strum timing — a downstream rule still has to schedule strums. We'd be solving the easier half of the problem twice.
60	- **Shape D — two-head (continuous fret + sparse strum events).** One head for held-note state, one head for `[time-to-strum, mask, dir]` events. Closer to the underlying physics. Rejected as v1 because it's significantly more complex to architect, train, and validate. **Worth revisiting if the per-bit-independence loss in the current shape produces poor strum timing in phase 2** — D's sparse-event head is a natural cure.
61
```

295	    )

298	
299	@dataclass(frozen=True)
300	class Actuator:
301	    """Emitted on every FretboardLink_Send call (one per producer intent).
302	
303	    `producer_id` is the arbitration signal that's invisible from the wire
304	    byte alone — when manual_control takes the wire from timing_pipeline,
305	    nothing about the byte itself changes. `last_ack_*` snapshot the most
306	    recent CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE so host can compute Send-to-ack latency
307	    without joining FBL_SEND/CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE stamps.
308	    """
309	
310	    hdr: Header
311	    intended_mask: int
312	    asserted_mask: int
313	    strum_dir: int        # 0=none, 1=down, 2=up
314	    producer_id: int      # ActuatorProducer value
315	    last_ack_result: int  # USB_HOST_CDC_RESULT_*, signed
316	    last_ack_ts_counter: int
317	
318	    _BODY: ClassVar[struct.Struct] = struct.Struct("<BBBBiQ")
319	    SIZE: ClassVar[int] = HDR_SIZE + _BODY.size  # 16 + 16 = 32
320	
321	    @property
322	    def producer_name(self) -> str:
323	        try:
324	            return ActuatorProducer(self.producer_id).name.lower()
325	        except ValueError:
326	            return f"producer_{self.producer_id}"
327	
328	
329	@dataclass(frozen=True)
330	class FretboardRaw:
331	    """One parsed 12-byte fretboard data frame (firmware/fretboard).
332	
333	    `adc` is a 5-tuple of 12-bit unsigned ADC samples (0–4095, lower means
334	    a brighter sensor) ordered by `fret_t`: green, red, yellow, blue, orange.
335	
336	    At ~240 Hz fretboard rate against 60 Hz video, the same `frame_epoch`
337	    tags ~4 consecutive records — `hdr.ts_counter` (stamped at producer
338	    emit time) gives sub-frame ordering for offline join against
339	    `Detector` records.
340	    """
341	
342	    hdr: Header
343	    adc: tuple[int, ...]   # length FRET_COUNT, indexed by fret_t
344	
345	    _BODY: ClassVar[struct.Struct] = struct.Struct("<HHHHHH")  # 5×u16 + reserved
346	    SIZE: ClassVar[int] = HDR_SIZE + _BODY.size  # 16 + 12 = 28
347	
348

351	    hdr: Header
352	    raw: bytes

356	MAX_RECORD_BYTES = STRIP_HDR_BYTES + STRIP_MAX_BYTES  # 23068
357	
358	
359	# ─── Host→device commands ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
360	
361	# Bit n of the type-mask is RecordType value n. Bit 0 is unused.
362	RECORD_TYPE_BY_NAME: dict[str, int] = {rt.name: int(rt) for rt in RecordType}
363	
364	# Common preset masks used by the CLI.
365	TYPE_MASK_ALL = 0xFFFFFFFF
366	TYPE_MASK_MIN = (1 << RecordType.SESSION) | (1 << RecordType.DROP)

373	    """Pack a SET_TYPE_MASK command payload (no SOF/LEN/FCS framing)."""
374	    return _CMD_SET_MASK_FMT.pack(
375	        PERF_CMD_HDR_MAGIC, PERF_CMD_SET_TYPE_MASK, 0, mask & 0xFFFFFFFF
376	    )

1	"""Export a marvin-perf capture as a SensiML-compatible CSV for MPLAB ML.
2	
3	One row per PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW (~240 Hz). Each row carries the five raw
4	ADC values plus five binary labels (one per fret), where the label comes
5	from the most-recent PERF_REC_DETECTOR.pressed_mask broadcast forward by
6	frame_epoch (~4 fretboard samples per cv frame).
7	
8	CSV schema matches the MPLAB Data Visualizer "SensiML CSV" preset:
9	    timestamp,ph_green,ph_red,ph_yellow,ph_blue,ph_orange,
10	    label_green,label_red,label_yellow,label_blue,label_orange
11	
12	`timestamp` is decimal seconds since the SESSION record's ts_counter.
13	
14	Edge cases:
15	- FretboardRaw records before any Detector record are emitted with all
16	  labels = 0 by default; pass strict=True to drop them instead.
17	- Capture missing the SESSION record raises ExportError (no timer_freq_hz
18	  → no way to convert ts_counter to seconds).
19	"""
20	
21	from __future__ import annotations
22	
23	import csv
24	from dataclasses import dataclass
25	from pathlib import Path
26	
27	from ..capture import open_capture
28	from ..decode import decode_record
29	from ..framing import FrameStats, iter_frames
30	from ..records import Detector, FretboardRaw, Session
31	from ..transport import FileSource
32	
33	
34	_HEADER = (
35	    "timestamp",
36	    "ph_green", "ph_red", "ph_yellow", "ph_blue", "ph_orange",
37	    "label_green", "label_red", "label_yellow", "label_blue", "label_orange",
38	)
39	
40	
41	class ExportError(Exception):
42	    """Raised when a capture can't be exported (missing SESSION etc)."""
43	
44	
45	@dataclass(frozen=True)
46	class ExportStats:
47	    n_rows: int
48	    n_skipped_unlabeled: int
49	    n_detector_records: int
50	    n_fretboard_records: int
51	    t_start_s: float
52	    t_end_s: float
53	    timer_freq_hz: int
54	
55	    @property
56	    def duration_s(self) -> float:
57	        return self.t_end_s - self.t_start_s
58	
59	
60	def export_sensiml_csv(
61	    capture_path: str | Path,
62	    out_path: str | Path,
63	    *,
64	    strict: bool = False,
65	) -> ExportStats:
66	    """Read `capture_path`, write SensiML-format CSV to `out_path`.
67	
68	    `strict=True` drops FretboardRaw rows that arrive before the first
69	    Detector record (so every emitted row has a real label). Default is
70	    to emit them with all labels = 0 — useful when the capture starts
71	    before cv_marvin_v1 has produced its first frame.
72	    """
73	    capture = open_capture(capture_path)
74	
75	    session: Session | None = None
76	    last_detector: Detector | None = None
77	    n_skipped_unlabeled = 0
78	    n_detector_records = 0
79	    n_fretboard_records = 0
80	    n_rows = 0
81	    t_baseline: int | None = None  # ts_counter of the first emitted row
82	    t_end_s = 0.0
83	
84	    out_path = Path(out_path)
85	    with FileSource(capture.bin_path) as src, out_path.open("w", newline="") as fh:
86	        writer = csv.writer(fh)
87	        writer.writerow(_HEADER)
88	        stats = FrameStats()
89	
90	        for frame in iter_frames(src, stats):
91	            try:
92	                rec = decode_record(frame.payload)
93	            except Exception:
94	                continue
95	
96	            if isinstance(rec, Session) and session is None:
97	                session = rec
98	                continue
99	
100	            if isinstance(rec, Detector):
101	                last_detector = rec
102	                n_detector_records += 1
103	                continue
104	
105	            if isinstance(rec, FretboardRaw):
106	                n_fretboard_records += 1
107	                if session is None:
108	                    # No timer_freq_hz yet → can't write a real timestamp.
109	                    # Defer rejection to after the loop so we still tally
110	                    # how many records were skipped for diagnostics.
111	                    n_skipped_unlabeled += 1
112	                    continue
113	                if last_detector is None and strict:
114	                    n_skipped_unlabeled += 1
115	                    continue
116	
117	                if t_baseline is None:
118	                    t_baseline = rec.hdr.ts_counter
119	                t_s = (rec.hdr.ts_counter - t_baseline) / float(
120	                    session.timer_freq_hz
121	                )
122	                t_end_s = t_s
123	
124	                pressed = last_detector.pressed_mask if last_detector else 0
125	                row = [
126	                    f"{t_s:.6f}",
127	                    rec.adc[0], rec.adc[1], rec.adc[2], rec.adc[3], rec.adc[4],
128	                    (pressed >> 0) & 1,
129	                    (pressed >> 1) & 1,
130	                    (pressed >> 2) & 1,
131	                    (pressed >> 3) & 1,
132	                    (pressed >> 4) & 1,
133	                ]
134	                writer.writerow(row)
135	                n_rows += 1
136	
137	    if session is None:
138	        # Tear out the partial file before raising — exporting half a file
139	        # with no header is more confusing than an absent file.
140	        try:
141	            out_path.unlink()
142	        except FileNotFoundError:
143	            pass
144	        raise ExportError(
145	            f"capture {capture.path} has no SESSION record — cannot derive "
146	            "timer_freq_hz to compute timestamps"
147	        )
148	
149	    return ExportStats(
150	        n_rows=n_rows,
151	        n_skipped_unlabeled=n_skipped_unlabeled,
152	        n_detector_records=n_detector_records,
153	        n_fretboard_records=n_fretboard_records,
154	        t_start_s=0.0 if n_rows > 0 else 0.0,
155	        t_end_s=t_end_s,
156	        timer_freq_hz=session.timer_freq_hz,
157	    )
158

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-03 15:36:44Z)**_

Read the edge-ai docs, the rollout plan, and the current exporter/record schema. Here's where things actually stand.

## Short answer

Yes — a recording with **ACTUATOR + FRETBOARD_RAW** is the core input, **plus SESSION** (the exporter needs `timer_freq_hz` to turn `ts_counter` into timestamps, and bails with `ExportError` without it). DETECTOR is *not* strictly required for the actuator-label path, but you'll want it for sanity-checking.

But there are two things worth knowing before you record anything:

## 1. The recordings you have won't work

[captures/](tools/marvin-perf/captures/) only holds `web-*.csv` files — those are *already-exported, detector-labeled* SensiML CSVs (the old `--labels=detector` path). The actuator exporter consumes a **raw perf-log capture** (a `.bin` / capture dir with `perf.bin`), not a pre-exported CSV. So you need a fresh raw capture, recorded with the right type mask.

Minimum `PERF_CMD_SET_TYPE_MASK` for the actuator-label export:

| Record | Needed for | Strictly required? |
|---|---|---|
| `SESSION` (0x01) | `timer_freq_hz` → timestamps | **Yes** |
| `ACTUATOR` (0x0A) | the labels (`intended_mask`) | **Yes** |
| `FRETBOARD_RAW` (0x0B) | the 5 ADC features, one row each | **Yes** |
| `DETECTOR` (0x03) | sanity (compare `pressed_mask` vs `intended_mask`) | No, but recommended |

The rollout doc says enable all four ([rollout.md:9](tools/edge-ai/docs/rollout.md#L9), [training.md:46](tools/edge-ai/docs/training.md#L46)) — that's the safe call.

## 2. The exporter doesn't exist yet — and doesn't need a recording to *build*

Phase 1's deliverable is the `--labels=actuator` mode in [sensiml_csv.py](tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/exporters/sensiml_csv.py). Today that file only does the detector path (forward-fills `Detector.pressed_mask`), and `export_sensiml_csv()` doesn't even take a `--labels` arg yet — neither does the CLI ([cli.py:152](tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/cli.py#L152)). All the decoder pieces exist (`Actuator` at [records.py:299](tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/records.py#L299), `FretboardRaw` at [records.py:329](tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/records.py#L329)), so the work is purely in the exporter + CLI + tests.

**That code can be written and unit-tested against synthesized records** (the existing [test_export_sensiml_csv.py](tools/marvin-perf/tests/test_export_sensiml_csv.py) already builds fake captures in memory). So you don't need a real recording to land Phase 1's code — you only need a recording to do Phase 1's *verification* step (inspect a real CSV, confirm strum bits are sparse, frets dense).

## So, to start, you need:

1. **Nothing blocking the exporter** — I can build `--labels=actuator` now against synthetic test data.
2. **One real self-play capture** (`SESSION+ACTUATOR+FRETBOARD_RAW`, ideally +DETECTOR) to *validate* it — this is the one thing only you can produce (it needs marvin + the rig).
3. **Later, for Phase 2:** corpus variety (Easy/Medium/Expert, several songs) with one held-out song reserved — not needed yet.

One thing to confirm on your end: that marvin's firmware actually emits `ACTUATOR` and `FRETBOARD_RAW` into the perf-log when those mask bits are set (the schema slots exist at v3, but I haven't verified the producers are wired — I can check the firmware if you want).

Want me to start on the Phase 1 exporter (build + tests, synthetic data) while you go capture a self-play recording to validate against? If so I'd also spin up `tools/edge-ai/docs/journal.md` per the repo's journal convention, since this kicks off non-trivial multi-session work.

38	def _build_session_first(ts_counter: int = 0) -> bytes:
39	    """SESSION record body builder doesn't expose ts_counter; patch it in."""
40	    import struct
41	    from marvin_perf.records import PERF_LOG_HDR_MAGIC, RecordType, Session
42	
43	    hdr = struct.pack(
44	        "<HBBIQ", PERF_LOG_HDR_MAGIC, int(RecordType.SESSION), 0, 0, ts_counter
45	    )
46	    body = Session._BODY.pack(_TIMER_HZ, 3, 0, 0, 0)
47	    return hdr + body

50	def _make_capture(tmp_path: Path) -> Path:
51	    """A small synthetic capture covering the join paths.
52	
53	    Layout (timer_freq_hz=1 MHz so each ts_counter unit = 1 µs):
54	      SESSION                                                ts=0
55	      DETECTOR  epoch=1  pressed=0b00000  (no presses)       ts=10_000
56	      FRETBOARD_RAW × 4  epoch=1  adc=(100,200,...)          ts=10_000 + 0..3 ticks
57	      DETECTOR  epoch=2  pressed=0b00001  (green pressed)    ts=10_000 + 1 frame
58	      FRETBOARD_RAW × 4  epoch=2  adc=(50,...)               ts=...
59	      DETECTOR  epoch=3  pressed=0b00101  (green+yellow)     ts=...
60	      FRETBOARD_RAW × 4  epoch=3  adc=(40,...)               ts=...
61	
62	    First detector record arrives BEFORE the first fretboard record so the
63	    "skipped pre-detector" path is covered by a separate test.
64	    """
65	    payloads: list[bytes] = [_build_session_first(ts_counter=0)]
66	
67	    base = 10_000
68	    schedule = [
69	        (1, 0b00000, (3900, 3950, 3850, 3900, 3900)),
70	        (2, 0b00001, (1200, 3940, 3840, 3890, 3890)),  # green pressed → low
71	        (3, 0b00101, (1100, 3935, 1500, 3885, 3885)),  # green + yellow
72	    ]
73	    for i, (epoch, pressed, adc) in enumerate(schedule):
74	        det_ts = base + i * _TS_PER_FRAME
75	        payloads.append(
76	            build_detector_payload(
77	                frame_epoch=epoch,
78	                pressed_mask=pressed,
79	                edge_active_mask=0,
80	            )
81	        )
82	        for k in range(4):
83	            fb_ts = det_ts + k * _TS_PER_FRETBOARD
84	            payloads.append(
85	                build_fretboard_raw_payload(
86	                    frame_epoch=epoch, ts_counter=fb_ts, adc=adc
87	                )
88	            )
89	
90	    return _write_capture(tmp_path, payloads)

144	def cmd_export_ml(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
145	    """Export a finished capture as a SensiML-format CSV for MPLAB ML.
146	
147	    One row per fretboard ADC sample (~240 Hz); each row carries the five
148	    raw 12-bit ADC values plus five binary labels (one per fret) drawn
149	    from the most-recent cv_marvin_v1 detector record's pressed_mask.
150	    """
151	    try:
152	        stats = export_sensiml_csv(args.capture, args.out, strict=args.strict)
153	    except ExportError as e:
154	        print(f"export-ml: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
155	        return 1
156	    print(
157	        f"wrote {args.out}: {stats.n_rows} rows over {stats.duration_s:.2f} s "
158	        f"({stats.n_detector_records} detector records, "
159	        f"{stats.n_fretboard_records} fretboard records, "
160	        f"{stats.n_skipped_unlabeled} skipped)",
161	        file=sys.stderr,
162	    )
163	    # Loud failure modes: a structurally-valid CSV with zero usable labels is
164	    # training-useless and easy to miss from a one-line summary. Surface as a
165	    # warning the user can't ignore, and exit non-zero so scripts notice.
166	    if stats.n_rows > 0 and stats.n_detector_records == 0:
167	        print(
168	            "WARNING: capture contains no DETECTOR records — every row's "
169	            "label_* columns are all zeros. The CSV is unlabelled and not "
170	            "useful for training. Re-record with both DETECTOR and "
171	            "FRETBOARD_RAW enabled in the Types panel (or "
172	            "--types DETECTOR,FRETBOARD_RAW for `marvin-perf record`).",
173	            file=sys.stderr,
174	        )
175	        return 2
176	    if stats.n_rows == 0:
177	        print(
178	            "WARNING: capture contains no FRETBOARD_RAW records — output "
179	            "CSV has only the header row. Re-record with FRETBOARD_RAW "
180	            "enabled.",
181	            file=sys.stderr,
182	        )
183	        return 2
184	    return 0

175	    return build_header(RecordType.STRIP, frame_epoch=frame_epoch) + body + bgr

177	
178	# ─── Frame wrapper (SOF + LEN + payload + FCS) ───────────────────────────────
179	
180	
181	def wrap_frame(payload: bytes, *, corrupt_fcs: bool = False) -> bytes:
182	    length = len(payload)
183	    length_bytes = struct.pack("<H", length)
184	    fcs = fletcher16(length_bytes + payload)
185	    if corrupt_fcs:
186	        fcs ^= 0xFFFF
187	    return SOF_BYTES + length_bytes + payload + struct.pack("<H", fcs)

```python
"""Export a marvin-perf capture as a SensiML-compatible CSV for MPLAB ML.

One row per PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW (~240 Hz). Each row carries the five raw
ADC values plus a set of binary labels whose meaning depends on `labels`:

- `labels="detector"` (default, back-compat): five per-fret labels drawn from
  the most-recent PERF_REC_DETECTOR.pressed_mask, broadcast forward by
  frame_epoch (~4 fretboard samples per cv frame). Columns:
      timestamp,ph_green,...,ph_orange,
      label_green,label_red,label_yellow,label_blue,label_orange
- `labels="actuator"` (edge-ai distillation target): six labels drawn from the
  most-recent PERF_REC_ACTUATOR.intended_mask — five frets verbatim plus one
  collapsed strum bit (logical OR of strum-down and strum-up, since alternating
  direction is a human ergonomic constraint the controller doesn't enforce).
  Columns:
      timestamp,ph_green,...,ph_orange,
      fret_green,fret_red,fret_yellow,fret_blue,fret_orange,strum

The collapse is a property of *this* exporter mode, not the raw capture:
PERF_REC_ACTUATOR keeps both strum bits as marvin emitted them, so a future
direction-aware corpus can preserve them. See tools/edge-ai/docs/training.md §2.

`timestamp` is decimal seconds since the first emitted row's ts_counter.

Edge cases:
- FretboardRaw records before the first label-source record (Detector or
  Actuator, depending on mode) are emitted with all labels = 0 by default;
  pass strict=True to drop them instead.
- Capture missing the SESSION record raises ExportError (no timer_freq_hz
  → no way to convert ts_counter to seconds).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import csv
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path

from ..capture import open_capture
from ..decode import decode_record
from ..framing import FrameStats, iter_frames
from ..records import Actuator, Detector, FretboardRaw, Session
from ..transport import FileSource


_HEADER_DETECTOR = (
    "timestamp",
    "ph_green", "ph_red", "ph_yellow", "ph_blue", "ph_orange",
    "label_green", "label_red", "label_yellow", "label_blue", "label_orange",
)

_HEADER_ACTUATOR = (
    "timestamp",
    "ph_green", "ph_red", "ph_yellow", "ph_blue", "ph_orange",
    "fret_green", "fret_red", "fret_yellow", "fret_blue", "fret_orange",
    "strum",
)

LABEL_MODES = ("detector", "actuator")


class ExportError(Exception):
    """Raised when a capture can't be exported (missing SESSION etc)."""


def _collapse_strum(intended_mask: int) -> int:
    """Collapse the 7-bit wire byte's two strum bits into one.

    Bit 5 is strum-down, bit 6 is strum-up. The edge-ai model only learns
    *when* to strum, not direction, so the two collapse to a single bit.
    """
    return ((intended_mask >> 5) | (intended_mask >> 6)) & 1


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ExportStats:
    n_rows: int
    n_skipped_unlabeled: int
    n_detector_records: int
    n_fretboard_records: int
    t_start_s: float
    t_end_s: float
    timer_freq_hz: int
    labels: str = "detector"
    n_actuator_records: int = 0
    # Rising-edge count of the collapsed strum bit (actuator mode only): the
    # number of distinct strums in the corpus, for sanity against the song.
    n_strum_events: int = 0

    @property
    def duration_s(self) -> float:
        return self.t_end_s - self.t_start_s


def export_sensiml_csv(
    capture_path: str | Path,
    out_path: str | Path,
    *,
    labels: str = "detector",
    strict: bool = False,
) -> ExportStats:
    """Read `capture_path`, write SensiML-format CSV to `out_path`.

    `labels` selects the label source: "detector" (per-fret pressed_mask,
    default, back-compat) or "actuator" (5 frets + collapsed strum from
    Actuator.intended_mask — the edge-ai distillation target).

    `strict=True` drops FretboardRaw rows that arrive before the first
    label-source record (so every emitted row has a real label). Default is
    to emit them with all labels = 0 — useful when the capture starts before
    the label source has produced its first record.
    """
    if labels not in LABEL_MODES:
        raise ExportError(
            f"unknown labels mode {labels!r}; expected one of {LABEL_MODES}"
        )

    capture = open_capture(capture_path)

    session: Session | None = None
    last_detector: Detector | None = None
    last_actuator: Actuator | None = None
    n_skipped_unlabeled = 0
    n_detector_records = 0
    n_actuator_records = 0
    n_fretboard_records = 0
    n_rows = 0
    n_strum_events = 0
    prev_strum = 0
    t_baseline: int | None = None  # ts_counter of the first emitted row
    t_end_s = 0.0

    header = _HEADER_ACTUATOR if labels == "actuator" else _HEADER_DETECTOR

    out_path = Path(out_path)
    with FileSource(capture.bin_path) as src, out_path.open("w", newline="") as fh:
        writer = csv.writer(fh)
        writer.writerow(header)
        stats = FrameStats()

        for frame in iter_frames(src, stats):
            try:
                rec = decode_record(frame.payload)
            except Exception:
                continue

            if isinstance(rec, Session) and session is None:
                session = rec
                continue

            if isinstance(rec, Detector):
                last_detector = rec
                n_detector_records += 1
                continue

            if isinstance(rec, Actuator):
                last_actuator = rec
                n_actuator_records += 1
                continue

            if isinstance(rec, FretboardRaw):
                n_fretboard_records += 1
                if session is None:
                    # No timer_freq_hz yet → can't write a real timestamp.
                    # Defer rejection to after the loop so we still tally
                    # how many records were skipped for diagnostics.
                    n_skipped_unlabeled += 1
                    continue

                have_label = (
                    last_actuator is not None
                    if labels == "actuator"
                    else last_detector is not None
                )
                if not have_label and strict:
                    n_skipped_unlabeled += 1
                    continue

                if t_baseline is None:
                    t_baseline = rec.hdr.ts_counter
                t_s = (rec.hdr.ts_counter - t_baseline) / float(
                    session.timer_freq_hz
                )
                t_end_s = t_s

                adc = (
                    rec.adc[0], rec.adc[1], rec.adc[2], rec.adc[3], rec.adc[4],
                )
                if labels == "actuator":
                    mask = last_actuator.intended_mask if last_actuator else 0
                    strum = _collapse_strum(mask)
                    if strum and not prev_strum:
                        n_strum_events += 1
                    prev_strum = strum
                    row = [
                        f"{t_s:.6f}", *adc,
                        (mask >> 0) & 1,
                        (mask >> 1) & 1,
                        (mask >> 2) & 1,
                        (mask >> 3) & 1,
                        (mask >> 4) & 1,
                        strum,
                    ]
                else:
                    pressed = last_detector.pressed_mask if last_detector else 0
                    row = [
                        f"{t_s:.6f}", *adc,
                        (pressed >> 0) & 1,
                        (pressed >> 1) & 1,
                        (pressed >> 2) & 1,
                        (pressed >> 3) & 1,
                        (pressed >> 4) & 1,
                    ]
                writer.writerow(row)
                n_rows += 1

    if session is None:
        # Tear out the partial file before raising — exporting half a file
        # with no header is more confusing than an absent file.
        try:
            out_path.unlink()
        except FileNotFoundError:
            pass
        raise ExportError(
            f"capture {capture.path} has no SESSION record — cannot derive "
            "timer_freq_hz to compute timestamps"
        )

    return ExportStats(
        n_rows=n_rows,
        n_skipped_unlabeled=n_skipped_unlabeled,
        n_detector_records=n_detector_records,
        n_fretboard_records=n_fretboard_records,
        t_start_s=0.0,
        t_end_s=t_end_s,
        timer_freq_hz=session.timer_freq_hz,
        labels=labels,
        n_actuator_records=n_actuator_records,
        n_strum_events=n_strum_events,
    )

```

# marvin — Working Journal

Running log of planning, decisions, open questions, and work-in-progress for marvin. Newest entries at the top. For *what marvin is* (purpose, subsystems, interfaces, milestones), read [`spec.md`](spec.md) — this journal does not duplicate it.

---

## Current focus

**M1 — Reference detector v0.** First CV detector running on captured frames, publishing `detector_state_t` records onto the detector-state bus. No actuation yet. See [`spec.md`](spec.md) §4.2 for subsystem detail and §8 for the milestone progression.

Scaffold is in place as of 2026-05-20: `detector/detector.{h,c}` owns the bus queue + a temporary drain task that logs records-per-second; `detector/cv_marvin_v1.{h,c}` subscribes to the video frame queue and publishes one `detector_state_t` per frame with `frame_epoch = Video_FrameInfo.frame_count` and all-zero fret state. Next: pick the v0 algorithm (Q8) and start populating `fret[]`.

**Capture/display pipeline is done as of 2026-05-02:** source → TC358743 → CSI-2 @ 972 Mbps/lane → SAM9X75 → ISC DMA → DDR (BGRX32) → XLCDC OVR1 → LVDSC → 10.1″ 1280×800 LVDS panel.

> **Deeper-dive references:**
> - [`spec.md`](spec.md) — system-level spec (read first).
> - [`capture_pipeline.md`](capture_pipeline.md) — HDMI → DDR capture stage (CSI2DC, ISC, register settings, datasheet citations).
> - [`display_path.md`](display_path.md) — DDR → LCD display stage (XLCDC OVR1 wiring, pillarbox, cache coherence).

> **Earlier entries** (capture/display bring-up, 2026-05-01 → 2026-05-15) are preserved in [`journal-archive.md`](journal-archive.md).

No `PERF_LOG_SCHEMA_VERSION` bump — additive only. | Step 1 of the Edge-AI training-dataset workstream: `cv_marvin_v1` provides the reference label per video frame, fretboard ADC samples are the input the future Edge-AI MCU would see. Routing both signals through the perf log lets one offline tool join them on `frame_epoch` (~4 fretboard records per video frame) and `ts_counter` (sub-frame ordering), which is the cheapest path to a labelled dataset before the SD recorder (§4.6) exists. Sibling task instead of folding RX into `fretboard_link_task` keeps the existing TX path untouched (its `xQueueReceive` blocking shape doesn't compose with a stream buffer without bigger surgery). The downstream `adc_fretboard` detector (§4.2, M2) is the natural follow-up; the bus scaffold (`DETECTOR_ADC_FRETBOARD = 1`) is already reserved. |

The previous comment ("fretboard side ignores baud over USB CDC") was wrong; only matters that the *application* on the PIC32 doesn't see the CDC line-coding fields, but the EDBG bridge in between very much does. `tools/fret-tuner/actuator.py` still hardcodes `ACTUATOR_BAUDRATE = 115200` for the same physical link — flagged as a follow-up; out of scope for this commit (different subproject). |

New helper `F_DRV_USB_UDPHS_DEVICE_ArmDmaForIrp` called after queue advance in `Tasks_ISR_DMA` and the ZLP-completion path. Logged as patch #9. | Stock Harmony USB v3.16.0 driver only programs the DMA channel in `IRPSubmit`'s queue-empty branch — IRPs appended to a non-empty queue link in the linked list but never get armed for transmission. Without this, `queueSizeWrite > 1` accepts writes but only ever transmits the first of any batch — we'd accept three perf-log strips, transmit one, the other two stranded forever. The IRP-queue infrastructure is *already there* in the driver, the missing piece is the post-completion arm. Fix is additive (new helper, two new call sites, no refactor of existing IRPSubmit body), making it easy to find/maintain after MCC regen. Future Harmony versions may obviate this if upstream wires it up. |
| 2026-05-29 | Strip queue uses 1-byte slot indices into a static `s_strip_pool[depth+2]` instead of pass-by-value `perf_rec_strip_t` items. | FreeRTOS queues are pass-by-value: every `xQueueSend`/`xQueueReceive` does `memcpy(slot, src, item_size)` inside a critical section (interrupts disabled). At `sizeof(perf_rec_strip_t) = 23-61 KB`, that was 38-100 µs of interrupts-off time per queue op × ~240 ops/s. Pool-and-index pattern moves the pixel data into a static pool indexed by 1-byte handles; queue ops drop to 1 µs critical sections. Same total BSS footprint (eliminates the producer's `static r;` and drain's `static s_strip_drain;` — pool size matches old "queue + 2 staging" footprint). Pool size `depth + 2` covers "1 slot in producer's hand + 1 in drain's hand" while preserving drop-on-full semantics. |
| 2026-05-29 | Fletcher-16 (mod 255, init 0xFFFF) replaces CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE in the framing layer. `crc_*` field names renamed to `fcs_*` end-to-end. | USB hardware already CRCs every bulk packet on the wire; our framing-layer checksum's job is *firmware-side framing-bug detection* and *resync alignment* (false SOF in the middle of a corrupt stream). Fletcher-16 catches single-byte changes, adjacent swaps, and most non-adjacent swaps with ~1/65536 false-positive rate against random byte streams — sufficient for that job at ~2 cycles/byte (vs ~25 cycles for the bit-by-bit CRC, ~6 cycles for table-driven). SAM9X75 has no CRCCU peripheral (verified against `packs/SAM9X75D2G_DFP/component/`), so DMA-driven CRC isn't available. Wire format unchanged (still SOF+LEN+payload+16-bit checksum). One-shot wire-format break — old `.bin` captures aren't readable with new code; fine for dev. |

Real binding constraint is the wire LEN field, which is `uint16_t` → max 65535 byte payload → max ~65 KB pixel per strip. Tighter than the UDPHS DMA cap (128 KB at `DRV_USB_UDPHS_DMA_MAX_TRANSFER_SIZE = 2`). Picking 65000 lands just under the LEN cap with margin. Producer accepts any (w, h) shape under that — practical envelope at 60 fps: 720×30, 480×45, 320×64, 290×72. Going beyond requires bumping LEN to u32, which is a wire-format break and not worth doing casually since wire bandwidth caps out around the same point at 60 fps. |
| 2026-05-29 | Default-disable high-rate perf-log record types at firmware boot — start mask is `DROP | TASK_HIGHWATER | TASK_RUNTIME` only; STAMP, DETECTOR, TIMING, STRIP off until host enables. | Avoids the unattended-firmware case where boot generates multi-MB/s of strip records that all get dropped at the sink (no DTR), burning producer-side CPU on framing/Fletcher work that goes nowhere. Host viewer enables higher-rate types via `PERF_CMD_SET_TYPE_MASK` on attach (the live mode's mask UI). SESSION is always emitted regardless of mask so the host gets `timer_freq_hz` on attach. |

MCC tasks re-prioritised via the per-component yml files so future regens preserve the layout. | Pre-change layout had 11 tasks bunched at priority 1 (9 MCC pollers + VideoTask + DetectorDrain) and 4 at priority 2, with no headroom. Two concrete problems: (a) VideoTask was *below* its consumer CvMarvinV1, a classic priority inversion that would bite during any priority-2 busy spell; (b) Legato (UI rendering) at the same priority as USB host driver tasks meant a heavy frame redraw could stall fretboard wire transit. The new layout puts strum-critical output above vision-real-time above diagnostic-I/O above UI, which matches the failure-cost ordering: a late strum is a missed note, a late detector tick recovers next frame, a late UI paint is jitter only. Reserve bands cost ~60 B BSS each, leave room for future watchdog or fault-recovery work to land without re-shuffling. Setting priorities in MCC yml (rather than patching `tasks.c` post-regen) avoids a re-apply patch — the source of truth and the emitted code now agree. |

# edge-ai — Working Journal

Running log of planning, decisions, open questions, and work-in-progress for the edge-ai distillation effort. Newest entries at the top. For *what edge-ai is* (purpose, the distillation shape, phased rollout), read [`SPEC.md`](SPEC.md) and the doc map there — this journal does not duplicate it.

---

## Current focus

**Phase 1 — Data pipeline.** Get distillation labels available end-to-end: a `--labels=actuator` export mode in [`tools/marvin-perf`](../../marvin-perf/) that turns a marvin self-play perf-log capture into a SensiML CSV of `5 ADC + 5 fret + 1 collapsed-strum` per row. See [`rollout.md`](rollout.md) for the phase definitions and verification gates.

Exporter code + tests landed 2026-06-03 (offline, no firmware change). The remaining Phase-1 gate is the *verification* step: run the new mode against a real self-play capture and confirm row count ≈ 240 × duration, strum bits sparse, fret bits dense and matching difficulty. That needs a real recording (see open questions).

---

## Decision log

| Date | Decision | Rationale |
|------|----------|-----------|
| 2026-06-03 | Phase 1 exporter implemented as a `--labels={detector,actuator}` switch on the existing `export-ml` command rather than a new subcommand. Default stays `detector` (back-compat); `actuator` emits the `fret_*,strum` schema. | The two modes share the whole capture-read / timestamp / forward-fill loop; only the label-source record (`Detector` vs `Actuator`) and the output columns differ. A flag keeps one code path and one set of edge-case handling (missing SESSION, pre-label rows, strict mode). The detector path's CSV bytes are unchanged, so the existing corpus/tooling keeps working. |
| 2026-06-03 | `n_strum_events` stat counts **rising edges** (0→1 transitions) of the collapsed strum bit, not strum-active rows. | "Events" = distinct strums, which is the quantity to sanity-check against a song's note count. Per-row density ("a few %") is still eyeballable from the CSV; the rising-edge count is the more information-dense single number and doesn't conflate hold-duration with strum count. |
| 2026-06-03 | Collapsed strum bit computed from `Actuator.intended_mask` bits 5\|6 (the doc formula), not from the separate `strum_dir` field. | `intended_mask` is the actual 7-bit wire byte marvin sent (`FretboardLink_Send` value at [fretboard_link.c:430](../../../firmware/marvin/default/src/actuator/fretboard_link.c#L430)); distilling against the byte-on-the-wire is the whole point. `strum_dir` is a redundant convenience enum. Using the mask keeps the label = exactly what fretboard saw. |
| 2026-06-03 | ACTUATOR producer wiring confirmed present in marvin firmware before building the exporter. | `PerfLog_EmitActuator` is called unconditionally inside `FretboardLink_Send` ([fretboard_link.c:430](../../../firmware/marvin/default/src/actuator/fretboard_link.c#L430)), which both `timing_pipeline` and `manual_control` drive. So any self-play capture with the `ACTUATOR` (0x0A) mask bit set carries `intended_mask` + `strum_dir` per Send — no firmware work needed for Phase 1. |

(Higher-level locked decisions — output shape, distillation supervision, deployment target — live in [`SPEC.md` §3](SPEC.md).)

---

> Phase-1-blocking items first; the design forks for phase 2+ live in [`review.md`](review.md).

- **Need a real self-play capture to close the Phase-1 gate.** The exporter is verified against synthetic records, but the rollout's Phase-1 "done when" requires inspecting one real captured-gameplay CSV. Required record types in the capture's `PERF_CMD_SET_TYPE_MASK`: `SESSION` + `ACTUATOR` + `FRETBOARD_RAW` (the exporter strictly needs only these three); `DETECTOR` recommended for cross-checking `pressed_mask` vs `intended_mask`. The existing files in [`tools/marvin-perf/captures/`](../../marvin-perf/captures/) are *already-exported detector CSVs*, not raw `.bin` captures, so they can't be re-exported through the actuator path — a fresh raw capture is needed.
- **Corpus variety for Phase 2.** Easy/Medium/Expert + song variety, with one held-out song reserved and reused across iterations. Not blocking Phase 1.

`PerfLog_EmitActuator` fires unconditionally inside `FretboardLink_Send` ([fretboard_link.c:430](firmware/marvin/default/src/actuator/fretboard_link.c#L430)), which both `timing_pipeline` and `manual_control` drive. So any self-play recording with the `ACTUATOR` (0x0A) mask bit enabled carries `intended_mask` (the 7-bit wire byte) + `strum_dir` on every Send. **No firmware work needed for Phase 1.**

## Phase 1 exporter built (offline, no firmware change)

- [sensiml_csv.py](tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/exporters/sensiml_csv.py) — new `--labels=actuator` mode. Schema `timestamp, ph_green…ph_orange, fret_green…fret_orange, strum`. Forward-fills `Actuator.intended_mask`, collapses strum-down|strum-up → one bit per the doc formula, reports `n_actuator_records` + `n_strum_events`. Default `detector` mode is byte-for-byte unchanged.
- [conftest.py](tools/marvin-perf/tests/conftest.py) — added `build_actuator_payload`.
- [cli.py](tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/cli.py) — `--labels {detector,actuator}` arg, mode-aware summary line, and a loud "no ACTUATOR records → unlabelled CSV" warning (exit 2).

**Tests: 90 passed** (the 2 viewer tests need the optional `fastapi` dep group — pre-existing, excluded). CLI smoke test confirmed end-to-end output + exit codes.

- 20,961 rows are >10 ms apart (gaps between clusters)
- **Zero** rows near the expected uniform 4.17 ms spacing

That's ~2.9 samples per burst every ~12 ms. The cause: `FretboardRaw.hdr.ts_counter` is stamped at **marvin's RX/emit time**, not when the fretboard physically sampled. USB CDC delivers the 240 Hz stream in bursts, so the RX task drains ~3 buffered frames back-to-back (µs apart), then waits ~12 ms for the next USB transfer. The samples themselves are real and in order — only their *timestamps* cluster.

**Two implications for Phase 2:**

1. **Window by row index, not by timestamp.** 60 consecutive rows = one 250 ms window, because each row is exactly one true fretboard sample at the fixed 240 Hz cadence. If anyone slices "250 ms of history" off the `timestamp` column instead, the burstiness will give wildly wrong window lengths. The `timestamp` column is good for plotting/duration, not for windowing.

2. **Minor label skew.** Because a sample taken at time T is logged at T+δ (δ up to one burst ≈ 12 ms / ~3 samples), forward-filling the active command can mis-assign by up to a burst near command transitions. This is exactly the "CDC + RTOS jitter in labels" risk already called out in [review.md](tools/edge-ai/docs/review.md) — tolerable for v1, worth measuring in Phase 2.

Neither is a bug in the exporter — the labels and ADC values are correct; it's a property of how the fretboard stream is timestamped. None of it blocks Phase 1.

Want me to log this timestamp-burstiness finding in the edge-ai journal (it's material for how Phase 2 builds windows)? And do you want me to add a quick `--stats`-style sanity dump to the exporter, or is the manual `awk` inspection enough for now?

## On the tooling question — I agree with your instinct: PyTorch-first, MPLAB ML as a later parallel demo

The docs currently say the opposite ([training.md §5.1](tools/edge-ai/docs/training.md#L52): "MPLAB ML / SensiML auto-pipeline first… fallback if auto-pipeline misses strum timing: tiny causal 1D-CNN"). I think inverting that is the right call, and not just for speed. The reasoning:

1. **The hard part is temporal, and that's exactly SensiML's weak spot.** The whole point of this design ([SPEC §3](tools/edge-ai/docs/SPEC.md#L42)) is that the model must learn the photo-dip→strum delay over a causal window — a *sequence* problem. SensiML's AutoML is feature-extraction + tree/ensemble over windowed stats; strong at "classify this window," weaker at learning event timing. We already wrote down that we'd fall back to a causal 1D-CNN if the auto-pipeline misses strum timing — so we're likely to end up hand-rolling the architecture anyway. Starting there skips a disappointing detour.

2. **The #1 hyperparameter is a sweep.** [review.md Q3](tools/edge-ai/docs/review.md) flags window length (125/250/400 ms) as the most important knob, and the sparse-strum class needs custom weighting (we now have a real number: **~5.8% strum density** from the capture → ~15–20× positive weight or focal loss). Both are one-liners in PyTorch and awkward in a GUI.

3. **Phase 2 is a research gate, not a product.** The rollout asks a reviewer to look at per-bit accuracy + a strum-timing distribution + a visual side-by-side and decide "worth porting?" That's all custom analysis code — trivial in Python.

**The honest cost of going programmatic:** we own int8 quantization and the on-device inference C in Phase 3 (MPLAB ML would have generated a deployable Knowledge Pack for us). But for a ≲1k-MAC, 2-conv-layer model on an M0+, hand-rolling int8 conv inference is genuinely small and tractable — and we keep bit-exact control, which the Phase-3 gate ("on-device matches host inference bit-for-bit") actually wants.

MPLAB ML stays valuable as an **eventual demonstration** — once we have clean labelled CSVs (which we now produce) and a known-good model shape, feeding the same data through the suite to show "here's the Microchip-tooling path, and here's how it compares" is a strong educational deliverable. Parallel track, not critical path.

- **Loss:** weighted BCE (strum weighted by the measured imbalance), focal as a backup.
- **Eval:** per-bit accuracy/F1 + strum-event timing error (match predicted vs true rising edges within tolerance; p95 against the 20 ms gate) + a 30 s predicted-vs-true plot.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-03 16:21:55Z)**_

You've hit on something real, and it's sharper than what the docs currently say. Let me lay out why I think you're right, then there's one choice that affects what you record next.

## Your instinct is correct — and it's an *observability* problem, not just a coverage one

The docs already flag multi-difficulty as a risk ([review.md](tools/edge-ai/docs/review.md): "Expert scrolls faster — photo dip is closer to the strum") but they frame the cure as "just train on all difficulties." Your point exposes why that cure is wrong if scroll speed actually varies:

marvin's strum timing is a **fixed** +220 ms after the note crosses *its* CV row (`y=311`). The photoxistors sit at a *different* row. So the delay the model must learn is:

```
photo-dip → strum  =  (pixel gap between photo row and CV row) / scroll_speed  +  220 ms
```

That first term is **inversely proportional to scroll speed**. If Expert scrolls faster, the same photo-dip pattern maps to a *shorter* delay than on Easy. With 5 sensors at one row and no difficulty input, the model can't tell which regime it's in — identical inputs, different correct outputs. Mixing difficulties would make it an ill-posed regression and the model would just average the delays, timing strums wrong on *both*. You can't fix that with more data; the information isn't observable.

(There's a weak escape hatch — dip *width* shrinks as scroll speed rises, so a wide window could in principle infer speed — but betting a tiny int8 model on that is fragile. Not for v1.)

## So: lock v1 to a single difficulty — it's the low-regret move

- **If scroll speed varies by difficulty:** single-difficulty avoids the ill-posed problem entirely.
- **If it turns out constant** (some rhythm games only change note *density*, not scroll speed): we lose nothing — we can merge difficulties later for free, and the extra data only helps.

Either way, starting single-difficulty is correct. And the eventual structure, *if* speed varies, is **one model per difficulty** with difficulty selected at runtime — marvin's game-state controller ([marvin spec §4.8](firmware/marvin/docs/spec.md)) already knows the difficulty, so it can tell fretboard which model to load. That's a cleaner story than one confused model.

**Bonus from fixing difficulty:** the photo→strum lag becomes a *constant* we can **measure** by cross-correlating photo dips against strum events in the data — turning the review.md "sweep the window length" guesswork into a measurement that sizes the window precisely.

And we can cheaply *test your premise* later: record the same song on two difficulties and compare the measured lag. If it's the same, scroll speed is constant; if not, you've confirmed the per-difficulty structure.

So your corpus = **many songs at one fixed difficulty, one song held out.** One choice here drives what you record:

Options:

- **Medium** - Balanced note density and scroll speed. Safer for sensor spatial resolution, but fewer strum events per minute than Expert, so the sparse-class problem is a bit worse.
- **Easy** - Slowest scroll, simplest patterns. But longest photo→strum delay (needs the widest window) and the sparsest strum signal — the weakest training data of the three.

```text
44	## 4. Capture protocol
45	
46	A training corpus is a set of marvin self-play perf-log captures across difficulty levels (Easy, Medium, Expert) and song variety. Each capture must have all of `SESSION + DETECTOR + ACTUATOR + FRETBOARD_RAW` enabled in the `PERF_CMD_SET_TYPE_MASK`.
47	
48	A held-out song is reserved per session for offline validation; the same held-out set should be reused across training iterations so per-iteration metrics are comparable.
49	
50	## 5. Model
51	
52	### 5.1 Recommended baseline
53	
54	- **Input:** 5 ADC channels × 60 samples (250 ms causal window) @ 240 Hz, int16 → int8 after normalisation.
55	- **Output:** 6 sigmoids during training (independent BCE per bit) — 5 frets + 1 collapsed strum; thresholded to binary at deploy. The runtime stage maps the strum bit into the wire byte's bit 5 (strum-down); bit 6 stays 0.
56	- **Architecture:** MPLAB ML / SensiML auto-pipeline first — windowed feature extractor (MAV, std, slope, peak, simple FIR taps) feeding a gradient-boosted ensemble or tiny dense head. SensiML targets exactly this MCU class.
57	- **Fallback if auto-pipeline misses strum timing:** tiny causal 1D-CNN, two conv layers ~8 channels, kernel 5–7, dilation `[1, 4]`. Quantise to int8.
58	
59	### 5.2 Why 250 ms
60	
61	`TP_STRUM_DELAY_MS = 220` ([timing_pipeline.c:21](../../../firmware/marvin/default/src/actuator/timing_pipeline.c)). 60 samples × 4.17 ms = 250 ms gives ≈30 ms margin around the photo-dip-to-strum-bit relationship. Window length is the most important hyperparameter to sweep — see [review.md Q3](review.md#q3-look-ahead-vs-now-cast).
62	
63	### 5.3 Quantisation
64	
65	int8 weights, int16 activations during the conv layers, int8 at the output. The intended deployment target has no FPU; floating-point inference is a non-starter. If the offline phase chooses to revisit the deployment target, the quantisation choice may relax.
66	
67	## 6. Loss
68	
69	Independent BCE per output bit, weighted to compensate for class imbalance:
70	
71	- Fret bits are dense (often 1 for many ticks per chord); near-1:1 weighting works.
72	- The strum bit is sparse (≤2 ticks per chord, ~5% of samples); weight strongly to avoid the trivial "always 0" minimum. Focal loss is a sane alternative if simple weighting plateaus.
73	
74	If per-bit independence produces poor strum timing, switch to a multi-class head over common chord shapes — see [review.md §alternatives](review.md#12-alternatives-considered).
```
</details></tool-use>
