19	#define PL_DRAIN_PRIORITY       3u
20	
21	#define PL_STATE_QUEUE_DEPTH    1024u
22	#define PL_STRIP_QUEUE_DEPTH    4u
23	
24	/* Strip slots live in a static pool; the strip queue and free list carry
25	 * just slot indices. Pool size = queue depth + 2 leaves room for one slot
26	 * being filled by the producer and one being processed by the drain at
27	 * the moment the queue is full, preserving the old drop-on-queue-full
28	 * semantics without ever stalling either side. */
29	#define PL_STRIP_POOL_SIZE      (PL_STRIP_QUEUE_DEPTH + 2u)
30	
31	/* State-queue slot is sized to the largest small record. */
32	#define PL_STATE_SLOT_BYTES     (sizeof(perf_rec_state_slot_t))
33	
34	#define PL_DROP_REPORT_PERIOD_MS   1000u
35	#define PL_DRAIN_RX_TIMEOUT_MS     20u
36	
37	/* ─── Internal types ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
38	
39	/* Discriminated slot for the state queue. The drain task switches on
40	 * hdr.type and writes only the populated bytes. Sized to the largest
41	 * small record so all types fit in one slot — DETECTOR_CONFIG is by far
42	 * the largest at ~188 B; the others fit in 32-51 B. The slot grew with
43	 * v3; queue depth × slot size is still trivial against 240 MB DDR. */
44	typedef union
45	{
46	    perf_hdr_t                  hdr;
47	    perf_rec_session_t          session;
48	    perf_rec_stamp_t            stamp;
49	    perf_rec_detector_t         detector;
50	    perf_rec_timing_t           timing;
51	    perf_rec_drop_t             drop;
52	    perf_rec_task_highwater_t   hwm;
53	    perf_rec_task_runtime_t     runtime;
54	    perf_rec_detector_config_t  detector_config;
55	    perf_rec_actuator_t         actuator;
56	    perf_rec_fretboard_raw_t    fretboard_raw;
57	} perf_rec_state_slot_t;
58	
59	/* ─── Static storage ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
60	
61	static QueueHandle_t s_state_q;
62	static StaticQueue_t s_state_q_buf;
63	static uint8_t       s_state_q_storage[PL_STATE_QUEUE_DEPTH * sizeof(perf_rec_state_slot_t)];
64	
65	/* Strip pool: data lives here from producer fill through drain write to the
66	 * sink — no copy at queue ops. Both queues carry uint8_t slot indices. The
67	 * "in-flight" queue holds full slots awaiting drain; the "free" queue holds
68	 * available slots for the producer to claim. */
69	static perf_rec_strip_t s_strip_pool[PL_STRIP_POOL_SIZE];
70	
71	static QueueHandle_t s_strip_q;
72	static StaticQueue_t s_strip_q_buf;
73	static uint8_t       s_strip_q_storage[PL_STRIP_QUEUE_DEPTH * sizeof(uint8_t)];
74	
75	static QueueHandle_t s_strip_free_q;
76	static StaticQueue_t s_strip_free_q_buf;
77	static uint8_t       s_strip_free_q_storage[PL_STRIP_POOL_SIZE * sizeof(uint8_t)];
78	
79	static StackType_t   s_drain_stack[PL_DRAIN_STACK_WORDS];
80	static StaticTask_t  s_drain_tcb;
81	
82	#define PL_TASK_SLOT_COUNT  18u  /* one per perf_task_id_t — IDLE + 9 MCC slots + OTHER + FRETBOARD_RX */
83	static TaskHandle_t  s_task_handles[PL_TASK_SLOT_COUNT];
84	
85	static volatile uint32_t s_drop_state;
86	static volatile uint32_t s_drop_strip;
87	static volatile uint32_t s_drop_sink;
88	
89	static volatile bool s_running;
90	
91	/* Boot with only the cheap diagnostic types enabled: DROP (1 Hz),
92	 * TASK_HIGHWATER (~6/s), TASK_RUNTIME (~6/s). The host viewer enables
93	 * higher-rate types (STAMP, DETECTOR, TIMING, STRIP) via
94	 * PERF_CMD_SET_TYPE_MASK once it's ready to consume them. SESSION is
95	 * always emitted regardless of mask.
96	 *
97	 * Why default-off for the high-rate types — and STRIP especially:
98	 * before a host attaches and clears the wire, every emitted record
99	 * burns producer CPU (queue ops, framing, Fletcher) only to be dropped
100	 * at the sink for lack of DTR. STRIP at 60 Hz is the worst case
101	 * (multiple MB/s of pixel data thrown away) but STAMP isn't free either
102	 * (~700/s of state-queue traffic). */
103	static volatile uint32_t s_enabled_mask =
104	    (1u << PERF_REC_DROP) |
105	    (1u << PERF_REC_TASK_HIGHWATER) |
106	    (1u << PERF_REC_TASK_RUNTIME);
107	
108	static inline bool type_enabled(uint8_t type)
109	{
110	    if (type == PERF_REC_SESSION) { return true; }
111	    return (s_enabled_mask & (1u << type)) != 0u;
112	}
113	
114	/* ─── Header fill ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
115	
116	static inline void hdr_fill(perf_hdr_t *h, uint8_t type, uint8_t flags,
117	                            uint32_t frame_epoch)
118	{
119	    h->magic       = PERF_LOG_HDR_MAGIC;
120	    h->type        = type;
121	    h->flags       = flags;
122	    h->frame_epoch = frame_epoch;
123	    h->ts_counter  = SYS_TIME_Counter64Get();
124	}
125	
126	/* ─── Record-size dispatch ───────────────────────────────────────────────── */
127	
128	static uint16_t record_size(const perf_rec_state_slot_t *r)
129	{
130	    switch (r->hdr.type)
131	    {
132	        case PERF_REC_SESSION:         return (uint16_t)sizeof(perf_rec_session_t);
133	        case PERF_REC_STAMP:           return (uint16_t)sizeof(perf_rec_stamp_t);
134	        case PERF_REC_DETECTOR:        return (uint16_t)sizeof(perf_rec_detector_t);
135	        case PERF_REC_TIMING:          return (uint16_t)sizeof(perf_rec_timing_t);
136	        case PERF_REC_DROP:            return (uint16_t)sizeof(perf_rec_drop_t);
137	        case PERF_REC_TASK_HIGHWATER:  return (uint16_t)sizeof(perf_rec_task_highwater_t);
138	        case PERF_REC_TASK_RUNTIME:    return (uint16_t)sizeof(perf_rec_task_runtime_t);
139	        case PERF_REC_DETECTOR_CONFIG: return (uint16_t)sizeof(perf_rec_detector_config_t);
140	        case PERF_REC_ACTUATOR:        return (uint16_t)sizeof(perf_rec_actuator_t);
141	        case PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW:   return (uint16_t)sizeof(perf_rec_fretboard_raw_t);
142	        default:                       return (uint16_t)sizeof(perf_hdr_t);
143	    }
144	}
145	
146	/* Variable-length: queue slot is max-sized, but on the wire we send only
147	 * HDR + body + the actually-used pixel bytes. */
148	static uint16_t strip_record_size(const perf_rec_strip_t *r)
149	{
150	    uint32_t pix = (uint32_t)r->w * (uint32_t)r->h * PERF_STRIP_BPP;
151	    if (pix > PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES) { pix = PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES; }
152	    return (uint16_t)(PERF_STRIP_HDR_BYTES + pix);
153	}
154	
155	/* ─── Drain task ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
156	
157	static void emit_session_record(void)
158	{
159	    perf_rec_session_t r;
160	    memset(&r, 0, sizeof(r));
161	    hdr_fill(&r.hdr, PERF_REC_SESSION, 0u, 0u);
162	    r.timer_freq_hz  = SYS_TIME_FrequencyGet();
163	    r.schema_version = (uint16_t)PERF_LOG_SCHEMA_VERSION;
164	    PerfLogSinkCdc_WriteFramed(&r, (uint16_t)sizeof(r));
165	}
166	
167	static void emit_drop_record(void)
168	{
169	    perf_rec_drop_t r;
170	    memset(&r, 0, sizeof(r));
171	    hdr_fill(&r.hdr, PERF_REC_DROP, 0u, 0u);
172	    r.dropped_state = s_drop_state;
173	    r.dropped_strip = s_drop_strip;
174	    r.dropped_sink  = s_drop_sink;
175	    PerfLogSinkCdc_WriteFramed(&r, (uint16_t)sizeof(r));
176	}
177	
178	static void sample_and_emit_hwms(void)
179	{
180	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < PL_TASK_SLOT_COUNT; i++)
181	    {
182	        TaskHandle_t h = s_task_handles[i];
183	        if (h == NULL) { continue; }
184	        uint32_t words = (uint32_t)uxTaskGetStackHighWaterMark(h);
185	        PerfLog_EmitTaskHighwater((perf_task_id_t)i, words);
186	    }
187	}
188	
189	/* Map FreeRTOS eTaskState → wire enum. Same numeric ordering today, but
190	 * cast through this so a future RTOS-side enum reshuffle doesn't silently
191	 * skew the wire format. */
192	static perf_task_state_t map_task_state(eTaskState s)
193	{
194	    switch (s)
195	    {
196	        case eRunning:   return PERF_TASK_STATE_RUNNING;
197	        case eReady:     return PERF_TASK_STATE_READY;
198	        case eBlocked:   return PERF_TASK_STATE_BLOCKED;
199	        case eSuspended: return PERF_TASK_STATE_SUSPENDED;
200	        case eDeleted:   return PERF_TASK_STATE_DELETED;
201	        default:         return PERF_TASK_STATE_INVALID;
202	    }
203	}
204	
205	/* Sized to comfortably exceed total live task count: marvin owns ~7
206	 * (CV / detector-drain / timing / fretboard-link / video / perf-drain /
207	 * idle) plus MCC-driven tasks (XLCDC, MAXTOUCH, LEGATO, SYS_INPUT, USB
208	 * host EHCI/OHCI/HUB/CDC) — call it ≤ 20 today, bump if we ever overflow. */
209	#define PL_RUNTIME_TASK_BUF  24u
210	
211	static void sample_and_emit_runtimes(void)
212	{
213	    static TaskStatus_t buf[PL_RUNTIME_TASK_BUF];
214	    UBaseType_t n = uxTaskGetSystemState(buf, PL_RUNTIME_TASK_BUF, NULL);
215	
216	    uint64_t sum_all = 0u, sum_registered = 0u;
217	
218	    for (UBaseType_t k = 0u; k < n; k++)
219	    {
220	        const TaskStatus_t *t = &buf[k];
221	        sum_all += (uint64_t)t->ulRunTimeCounter;
222	
223	        for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < PL_TASK_SLOT_COUNT; i++)
224	        {
225	            if (s_task_handles[i] != t->xHandle) { continue; }
226	            sum_registered += (uint64_t)t->ulRunTimeCounter;
227	            PerfLog_EmitTaskRuntime((perf_task_id_t)i,
228	                                    map_task_state(t->eCurrentState),
229	                                    (uint8_t)t->uxCurrentPriority,
230	                                    (uint32_t)t->ulRunTimeCounter);
231	            break;
232	        }
233	    }
234	
235	    /* OTHER pseudo-slot: every cycle not accounted to a registered task
236	     * (including IDLE, which is registered). Lets the host close the
237	     * books — Σ per-window CPU% = 100. State/priority don't have a
238	     * single value here; emit READY/0 as harmless placeholders. */
239	    PerfLog_EmitTaskRuntime(PERF_TASK_OTHER,
240	                            PERF_TASK_STATE_READY,
241	                            0u,
242	                            (uint32_t)(sum_all - sum_registered));
243	}
244	
245	/* MCC tasks are created in SYS_Tasks() right before vTaskStartScheduler,
246	 * not at SYS_Initialize time — so the handles aren't lookup-able from
247	 * APP_Initialize where PerfLog_Start runs. Same goes for the FreeRTOS
248	 * idle task: xTaskGetIdleTaskHandle() returns NULL until vTaskStartScheduler
249	 * creates it. The drain task runs after the scheduler is up and all
250	 * SYS_Tasks() xTaskCreate calls have landed; it does both lookups here.
251	 *
252	 * Names match the pcName argument in default/tasks.c xTaskCreate calls.
253	 * If MCC ever renames one (regen risk), xTaskGetHandle returns NULL and
254	 * that slot stays unregistered — its CPU runtime falls into OTHER, and
255	 * the host viewer sees a flat-zero series for that task as a hint. */
256	static const struct
257	{
258	    perf_task_id_t id;
259	    const char    *name;
260	} s_mcc_task_names[] =
261	{
262	    { PERF_TASK_LEGATO,        "LEGATO_Tasks"        },
263	    { PERF_TASK_XLCDC,         "XLCDC_Tasks"         },
264	    { PERF_TASK_MAXTOUCH,      "DRV_MAXTOUCH_Tasks"  },
265	    { PERF_TASK_SYS_INPUT,     "SYS_INPUT_Tasks"     },
266	    { PERF_TASK_USB_DEVICE,    "USB_DEVICE_TASKS"    },
267	    { PERF_TASK_USB_HOST,      "USB_HOST_TASKS"      },
268	    { PERF_TASK_DRV_USB_UDPHS, "DRV_USB_UDPHS_TASKS" },
269	    { PERF_TASK_DRV_USB_HOST,  "DRV_USB_HOST_TASKS"  },
270	    { PERF_TASK_APP,           "APP_Tasks"           },
271	};
272	
273	static void register_post_scheduler_tasks(void)
274	{
275	    TaskHandle_t idle = xTaskGetIdleTaskHandle();
276	    if (idle != NULL)
277	    {
278	        PerfLog_RegisterTaskForHighwater(PERF_TASK_IDLE, idle);
279	    }
280	    else
281	    {
282	        LOG_WARN("PerfLog: idle task handle not available\r\n");
283	    }
284	
285	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < sizeof(s_mcc_task_names) / sizeof(s_mcc_task_names[0]); i++)
286	    {
287	        TaskHandle_t h = xTaskGetHandle(s_mcc_task_names[i].name);
288	        if (h != NULL)
289	        {
290	            PerfLog_RegisterTaskForHighwater(s_mcc_task_names[i].id, h);
291	        }
292	        else
293	        {
294	            LOG_WARN("PerfLog: MCC task '%s' not found\r\n", s_mcc_task_names[i].name);
295	        }
296	    }
297	}
298	
299	static void perf_log_drain_task(void *param)
300	{
301	    (void)param;
302	
303	    PerfLogSinkCdc_Initialize();
304	    register_post_scheduler_tasks();
305	    s_running = true;
306	
307	    TickType_t last_drop = xTaskGetTickCount();
308	    bool prev_connected = false;
309	
310	    for (;;)
311	    {
312	        bool now_connected = PerfLogSinkCdc_IsConnected();
313	        if (now_connected && !prev_connected)
314	        {
315	            emit_session_record();
316	        }
317	        prev_connected = now_connected;
318	
319	        perf_rec_state_slot_t srec;
320	        if (xQueueReceive(s_state_q, &srec,
321	                          pdMS_TO_TICKS(PL_DRAIN_RX_TIMEOUT_MS)) == pdTRUE)
322	        {
323	            PerfLogSinkCdc_WriteFramed(&srec, record_size(&srec));
324	            /* Drain all currently queued state records before moving on.
325	             * Strips cost ~5 ms apiece on the wire, so a one-state-per-
326	             * iteration loop runs at ~50 Hz under load — well below the
327	             * ~700 stamps/s production rate. Same shape as the strip
328	             * drain below. */
329	            while (xQueueReceive(s_state_q, &srec, 0) == pdTRUE)
330	            {
331	                PerfLogSinkCdc_WriteFramed(&srec, record_size(&srec));
332	            }
333	        }
334	
335	        /* Strip drain: dequeue slot index, write the slot's data via
336	         * pointer (no copy), return slot to the free pool. */
337	        uint8_t slot_idx;
338	        while (xQueueReceive(s_strip_q, &slot_idx, 0) == pdTRUE)
339	        {
340	            const perf_rec_strip_t *r = &s_strip_pool[slot_idx];
341	            PerfLogSinkCdc_WriteFramed(r, strip_record_size(r));
342	            (void)xQueueSend(s_strip_free_q, &slot_idx, 0);
343	        }
344	
345	        if ((xTaskGetTickCount() - last_drop) >= pdMS_TO_TICKS(PL_DROP_REPORT_PERIOD_MS))
346	        {
347	            last_drop = xTaskGetTickCount();
348	            emit_drop_record();
349	            sample_and_emit_hwms();
350	            sample_and_emit_runtimes();
351	        }
352	    }
353	}
354	
355	/* ─── Init ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
356	
357	void PerfLog_Initialize(void)
358	{
359	    s_state_q = xQueueCreateStatic(PL_STATE_QUEUE_DEPTH,
360	                                   sizeof(perf_rec_state_slot_t),
361	                                   s_state_q_storage,
362	                                   &s_state_q_buf);
363	    configASSERT(s_state_q != NULL);
364	
365	    s_strip_q = xQueueCreateStatic(PL_STRIP_QUEUE_DEPTH,
366	                                   sizeof(uint8_t),
367	                                   s_strip_q_storage,
368	                                   &s_strip_q_buf);
369	    configASSERT(s_strip_q != NULL);
370	
371	    s_strip_free_q = xQueueCreateStatic(PL_STRIP_POOL_SIZE,
372	                                        sizeof(uint8_t),
373	                                        s_strip_free_q_storage,
374	                                        &s_strip_free_q_buf);
375	    configASSERT(s_strip_free_q != NULL);
376	
377	    /* Seed the free list with all pool indices. */
378	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < PL_STRIP_POOL_SIZE; i++)
379	    {
380	        (void)xQueueSend(s_strip_free_q, &i, 0);
381	    }
382	}
383	
384	void PerfLog_Start(void)
385	{
386	    TaskHandle_t h = xTaskCreateStatic(perf_log_drain_task,
387	                                       "PerfDrain",
388	                                       PL_DRAIN_STACK_WORDS,
389	                                       NULL,
390	                                       PL_DRAIN_PRIORITY,
391	                                       s_drain_stack,
392	                                       &s_drain_tcb);
393	    PerfLog_RegisterTaskForHighwater(PERF_TASK_PERF_DRAIN, h);
394	    /* Idle handle isn't valid until vTaskStartScheduler creates the idle
395	     * task — registered from the drain task post-scheduler instead, see
396	     * register_post_scheduler_tasks. */
397	}
398	
399	void PerfLog_RegisterTaskForHighwater(perf_task_id_t id, TaskHandle_t handle)
400	{
401	    if ((unsigned)id >= PL_TASK_SLOT_COUNT) { return; }
402	    s_task_handles[id] = handle;
403	}
404	
405	bool PerfLog_IsRunning(void)
406	{
407	    return s_running;
408	}
409	
410	/* ─── Emit (task context) ────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
411	
412	/* Drop counters are RMW from both task (send_state, EmitPatch,
413	 * NoteSinkDrop) and ISR (EmitStampFromISR) contexts. ARM926 single-
414	 * issue makes a single 32-bit aligned store atomic, but the increment
415	 * is LDR/ADD/STR — an ISR firing between LDR and STR loses an increment.
416	 * Critical sections (which globally disable IRQs on this port) keep
417	 * the RMW indivisible. The counters are diagnostic, so the very brief
418	 * IRQ-off window is fine. */
419	static inline void counter_add_task(volatile uint32_t *p, uint32_t v)
420	{
421	    taskENTER_CRITICAL();
422	    *p += v;
423	    taskEXIT_CRITICAL();
424	}
425	
426	static inline void counter_add_isr(volatile uint32_t *p, uint32_t v)
427	{
428	    UBaseType_t s = taskENTER_CRITICAL_FROM_ISR();
429	    *p += v;
430	    taskEXIT_CRITICAL_FROM_ISR(s);
431	}
432	
433	static inline void send_state(const perf_rec_state_slot_t *slot)
434	{
435	    if (s_state_q == NULL) { return; }
436	    if (!type_enabled(slot->hdr.type)) { return; }
437	    if (xQueueSend(s_state_q, slot, 0) != pdTRUE)
438	    {
439	        counter_add_task(&s_drop_state, 1u);
440	    }
441	}
442	
443	void PerfLog_EmitStamp(perf_stage_t stage, uint32_t frame_epoch, uint32_t aux)
444	{
445	    perf_rec_state_slot_t slot;
446	    memset(&slot, 0, sizeof(slot));
447	    hdr_fill(&slot.stamp.hdr, PERF_REC_STAMP, 0u, frame_epoch);
448	    slot.stamp.stage_id = (uint8_t)stage;
449	    slot.stamp.aux      = aux;
450	    send_state(&slot);
451	}
452	
453	void PerfLog_EmitDetector(uint32_t frame_epoch,
454	                          const uint16_t hold_dist[FRET_COUNT],
455	                          const uint16_t edge_dist[FRET_COUNT],
456	                          uint8_t  pressed_mask,
457	                          uint8_t  edge_active_mask)
458	{
459	    perf_rec_state_slot_t slot;
460	    memset(&slot, 0, sizeof(slot));
461	    hdr_fill(&slot.detector.hdr, PERF_REC_DETECTOR, 0u, frame_epoch);
462	    memcpy(slot.detector.hold_dist, hold_dist, sizeof(slot.detector.hold_dist));
463	    memcpy(slot.detector.edge_dist, edge_dist, sizeof(slot.detector.edge_dist));
464	    slot.detector.pressed_mask     = pressed_mask;
465	    slot.detector.edge_active_mask = edge_active_mask;
466	    send_state(&slot);
467	}

469	void PerfLog_EmitTiming(uint32_t frame_epoch, const perf_timing_snapshot_t *s)
470	{
471	    if (s == NULL) { return; }
472	    perf_rec_state_slot_t slot;
473	    memset(&slot, 0, sizeof(slot));
474	    hdr_fill(&slot.timing.hdr, PERF_REC_TIMING, 0u, frame_epoch);
475	    slot.timing.now_ms               = s->now_ms;
476	    slot.timing.chord_open           = s->chord_open;
477	    slot.timing.chord_mask           = s->chord_mask;
478	    slot.timing.chord_age_ms         = s->chord_age_ms;
479	    slot.timing.note_q_count         = s->note_q_count;
480	    slot.timing.note_head_mask       = s->note_head_mask;
481	    slot.timing.note_tail_mask       = s->note_tail_mask;
482	    slot.timing.note_head_at_ms      = s->note_head_at_ms;
483	    slot.timing.strum_q_count        = s->strum_q_count;
484	    slot.timing.strum_head_mask      = s->strum_head_mask;
485	    slot.timing.strum_dir_next       = s->strum_dir_next;
486	    slot.timing.strum_head_at_ms     = s->strum_head_at_ms;
487	    slot.timing.frets_active         = s->frets_active;
488	    slot.timing.strum_active         = s->strum_active;
489	    slot.timing.release_pending_mask = s->release_pending_mask;
490	    slot.timing.publish_mask         = s->publish_mask;
491	    slot.timing.strum_release_at_ms  = s->strum_release_at_ms;
492	    slot.timing.release_min_at_ms    = s->release_min_at_ms;
493	    send_state(&slot);
494	}

496	void PerfLog_EmitDetectorConfig(const perf_rec_detector_config_t *cfg)
497	{
498	    if (cfg == NULL) { return; }
499	    perf_rec_state_slot_t slot;
500	    memset(&slot, 0, sizeof(slot));
501	    slot.detector_config = *cfg;
502	    hdr_fill(&slot.detector_config.hdr, PERF_REC_DETECTOR_CONFIG, 0u, 0u);
503	    send_state(&slot);
504	}
505	
506	void PerfLog_EmitActuator(uint8_t  intended_mask,
507	                          uint8_t  asserted_mask,
508	                          uint8_t  strum_dir,
509	                          uint8_t  producer_id,
510	                          int32_t  last_ack_result,
511	                          uint64_t last_ack_ts_counter)
512	{
513	    perf_rec_state_slot_t slot;
514	    memset(&slot, 0, sizeof(slot));
515	    hdr_fill(&slot.actuator.hdr, PERF_REC_ACTUATOR, 0u, 0u);
516	    slot.actuator.intended_mask       = intended_mask;
517	    slot.actuator.asserted_mask       = asserted_mask;
518	    slot.actuator.strum_dir           = strum_dir;
519	    slot.actuator.producer_id         = producer_id;
520	    slot.actuator.last_ack_result     = last_ack_result;
521	    slot.actuator.last_ack_ts_counter = last_ack_ts_counter;
522	    send_state(&slot);
523	}
524	
525	void PerfLog_EmitFretboardRaw(const uint16_t adc[FRET_COUNT], uint32_t frame_epoch)
526	{
527	    if (adc == NULL) { return; }
528	    perf_rec_state_slot_t slot;
529	    memset(&slot, 0, sizeof(slot));
530	    hdr_fill(&slot.fretboard_raw.hdr, PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW, 0u, frame_epoch);
531	    memcpy(slot.fretboard_raw.adc, adc, sizeof(slot.fretboard_raw.adc));
532	    send_state(&slot);
533	}
534	
535	void PerfLog_EmitTaskHighwater(perf_task_id_t id, uint32_t words)
536	{
537	    perf_rec_state_slot_t slot;
538	    memset(&slot, 0, sizeof(slot));
539	    hdr_fill(&slot.hwm.hdr, PERF_REC_TASK_HIGHWATER, 0u, 0u);
540	    slot.hwm.task_id = (uint8_t)id;
541	    slot.hwm.words   = words;
542	    send_state(&slot);
543	}
544	
545	void PerfLog_EmitTaskRuntime(perf_task_id_t id,
546	                             perf_task_state_t state,
547	                             uint8_t priority,
548	                             uint32_t run_time_counter)
549	{
550	    perf_rec_state_slot_t slot;
551	    memset(&slot, 0, sizeof(slot));
552	    hdr_fill(&slot.runtime.hdr, PERF_REC_TASK_RUNTIME, 0u, 0u);
553	    slot.runtime.task_id          = (uint8_t)id;
554	    slot.runtime.state            = (uint8_t)state;
555	    slot.runtime.priority         = priority;
556	    slot.runtime.run_time_counter = run_time_counter;
557	    send_state(&slot);
558	}
559	
560	/* Strip producer: claim a free slot from the pool, row-copy a w×h BGR888
561	 * region out of the strided source frame directly into the slot, then
562	 * enqueue just the slot index. No struct memcpy in the queue critical
563	 * section — only a 1-byte index transfer.
564	 *
565	 * Total pixel bytes (w*h*3) must fit the slot's bgr[] capacity
566	 * (PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES); per-axis shape is unconstrained beyond that.
567	 * Drop-on-pool-empty; counter incremented under critical section. */
568	void PerfLog_EmitStripFromFrame(uint32_t frame_epoch,
569	                                perf_strip_kind_t kind,
570	                                const uint8_t *frame, uint32_t frame_stride,
571	                                uint16_t x, uint16_t y,
572	                                uint16_t w, uint16_t h)
573	{
574	    if (s_strip_q == NULL || s_strip_free_q == NULL || frame == NULL) { return; }
575	    if (!type_enabled(PERF_REC_STRIP)) { return; }
576	    if (w == 0u || h == 0u) { return; }
577	    if ((uint32_t)w * (uint32_t)h * PERF_STRIP_BPP > PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES) { return; }
578	
579	    uint8_t slot_idx;
580	    if (xQueueReceive(s_strip_free_q, &slot_idx, 0) != pdTRUE)
581	    {
582	        counter_add_task(&s_drop_strip, 1u);
583	        return;
584	    }
585	
586	    perf_rec_strip_t *r = &s_strip_pool[slot_idx];
587	    memset(r, 0, PERF_STRIP_HDR_BYTES);
588	    hdr_fill(&r->hdr, PERF_REC_STRIP, 0u, frame_epoch);
589	    r->x    = x;
590	    r->y    = y;
591	    r->w    = w;
592	    r->h    = h;
593	    r->kind = (uint8_t)kind;
594	
595	    const uint32_t row_bytes = (uint32_t)w * PERF_STRIP_BPP;
596	    const uint8_t *src = frame + (uint32_t)y * frame_stride + (uint32_t)x * PERF_STRIP_BPP;
597	    uint8_t *dst = r->bgr;
598	    for (uint16_t row = 0u; row < h; row++)
599	    {
600	        memcpy(dst, src, row_bytes);
601	        src += frame_stride;
602	        dst += row_bytes;
603	    }
604	
605	    if (xQueueSend(s_strip_q, &slot_idx, 0) != pdTRUE)
606	    {
607	        /* In-flight queue full (pool sized depth+2 makes this rare; only
608	         * possible if the drain task is blocked while strip_q is at depth
609	         * and the producer also holds a slot). Return slot to free pool. */
610	        (void)xQueueSend(s_strip_free_q, &slot_idx, 0);
611	        counter_add_task(&s_drop_strip, 1u);
612	    }
613	}
614	
615	/* ─── Emit (ISR context) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
616	
617	void PerfLog_EmitStampFromISR(perf_stage_t stage,
618	                              uint32_t frame_epoch,
619	                              uint32_t aux,
620	                              BaseType_t *higher_priority_task_woken)
621	{
622	    if (s_state_q == NULL) { return; }
623	    if (!type_enabled(PERF_REC_STAMP)) { return; }
624	    perf_rec_state_slot_t slot;
625	    memset(&slot, 0, sizeof(slot));
626	    hdr_fill(&slot.stamp.hdr, PERF_REC_STAMP, PERF_FLAG_FROM_ISR, frame_epoch);
627	    slot.stamp.stage_id = (uint8_t)stage;
628	    slot.stamp.aux      = aux;
629	    if (xQueueSendFromISR(s_state_q, &slot, higher_priority_task_woken) != pdTRUE)
630	    {
631	        counter_add_isr(&s_drop_state, 1u);
632	    }
633	}
634	
635	/* ─── Sink-side drop accounting ──────────────────────────────────────────── */
636	
637	void PerfLog_NoteSinkDrop(uint32_t bytes_dropped)
638	{
639	    counter_add_task(&s_drop_sink, bytes_dropped);
640	}
641	
642	/* ─── Record-type filter ─────────────────────────────────────────────────── */

648	}
649

651	{
652	    return s_enabled_mask;
653	}

13	 * queues (small / patch); a low-priority drain task frames them
14	 * (SOF + length + payload + CRC-16/CCITT) and pushes the bytes out the
15	 * USB-device CDC sink. Drop-on-full, never block. The pipeline must
16	 * remain unaffected if perf-log vanishes.
17	 *
18	 * All emit calls take ≈O(memcpy) and never lock. The ISR variants use
19	 * xQueueSendFromISR; the task variants use xQueueSend with zero block
20	 * time. Choose by call site — passing the wrong one will not corrupt
21	 * state but may misuse the higher_priority_task_woken pathway. */

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class FretboardRaw:
    """One parsed 12-byte fretboard data frame (firmware/fretboard).

    `adc` is a 5-tuple of 12-bit unsigned ADC samples (0–4095, lower means
    a brighter sensor) ordered by `fret_t`: green, red, yellow, blue, orange.

    At ~240 Hz fretboard rate against 60 Hz video, the same `frame_epoch`
    tags ~4 consecutive records — `hdr.ts_counter` (stamped at producer
    emit time) gives sub-frame ordering for offline join against
    `Detector` records.

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Actuator:
    """Emitted on every FretboardLink_Send call (one per producer intent).

    `producer_id` is the arbitration signal that's invisible from the wire
    byte alone — when manual_control takes the wire from timing_pipeline,
    nothing about the byte itself changes. `last_ack_*` snapshot the most
    recent CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE so host can compute Send-to-ack latency
    without joining FBL_SEND/CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE stamps.
    """

    hdr: Header
    intended_mask: int
    asserted_mask: int
    strum_dir: int        # 0=none, 1=down, 2=up
    producer_id: int      # ActuatorProducer value
    last_ack_result: int  # USB_HOST_CDC_RESULT_*, signed
    last_ack_ts_counter: int

    _BODY: ClassVar[struct.Struct] = struct.Struct("<BBBBiQ")
    SIZE: ClassVar[int] = HDR_SIZE + _BODY.size  # 16 + 16 = 32
```

**_collapse_strum helper (lines 66-72):**
```python
def _collapse_strum(intended_mask: int) -> int:
    """Collapse the 7-bit wire byte's two strum bits into one.

    Bit 5 is strum-down, bit 6 is strum-up. The edge-ai model only learns
    *when* to strum, not direction, so the two collapse to a single bit.
    """
    return ((intended_mask >> 5) | (intended_mask >> 6)) & 1
```

```c
/* PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW — one record per parsed 12-byte fretboard data
 * frame (firmware/fretboard/data_stream.c). The 5×u16 ADC values are 12-bit
 * unsigned (0–4095, lower = brighter sensor) indexed by fret_t (G/R/Y/B/O).
 * Fretboard emits at ~240 Hz; with video at 60 Hz the same frame_epoch
 * value tags ~4 consecutive records — ts_counter (stamped by hdr_fill at
 * record-emit time) disambiguates within the frame. Default-disabled at
 * boot like the other high-rate types. */
typedef struct __attribute__((packed))
{
    perf_hdr_t hdr;
    uint16_t   adc[FRET_COUNT];      /* 5 × 2 = 10 B */
    uint16_t   reserved;
} perf_rec_fretboard_raw_t;
```

207	    if expected_pixels > STRIP_MAX_BYTES:
208	        raise DecodeError(
209	            f"Strip: w*h*bpp {expected_pixels} > max {STRIP_MAX_BYTES}"
210	        )
211	    expected_total = STRIP_HDR_BYTES + expected_pixels
212	    if len(payload) != expected_total:
213	        raise DecodeError(
214	            f"Strip: payload {len(payload)} != expected {expected_total} "
215	            f"({w}×{h}×{STRIP_BPP})"
216	        )
217	    bgr = bytes(payload[STRIP_HDR_BYTES:expected_total])
218	    return Strip(hdr=hdr, x=x, y=y, w=w, h=h, kind=kind, bgr=bgr)
219	
220	
221	_DISPATCH = {
222	    RecordType.SESSION: _decode_session,
223	    RecordType.STAMP: _decode_stamp,
224	    RecordType.DETECTOR: _decode_detector,
225	    RecordType.TIMING: _decode_timing,
226	    RecordType.DROP: _decode_drop,
227	    RecordType.TASK_HIGHWATER: _decode_task_highwater,
228	    RecordType.TASK_RUNTIME: _decode_task_runtime,
229	    RecordType.STRIP: _decode_strip,
230	    RecordType.DETECTOR_CONFIG: _decode_detector_config,
231	    RecordType.ACTUATOR: _decode_actuator,
232	    RecordType.FRETBOARD_RAW: _decode_fretboard_raw,
233	}
234	
235	
236	def decode_record(payload: bytes) -> Record:
237	    """Decode an FCS-validated frame payload into a typed Record dataclass.
238	
239	    Caller (framing.iter_frames) has already verified FCS and length sanity.
240	    Unknown record types are surfaced as UnknownRecord so a forward-schema
241	    firmware does not crash an older host.
242	    """
243	    if len(payload) < HDR_SIZE:
244	        raise DecodeError(f"payload {len(payload)} < HDR_SIZE {HDR_SIZE}")
245	    hdr = Header.unpack(payload)
246	    if hdr.magic != PERF_LOG_HDR_MAGIC:
247	        raise DecodeError(f"bad magic 0x{hdr.magic:04x}")
248	
249	    decoder = _DISPATCH.get(hdr.type)
250	    if decoder is None:
251	        return UnknownRecord(hdr=hdr, raw=payload)
252	    return decoder(hdr, payload)
253

1	"""Export a marvin-perf capture as a SensiML-compatible CSV for MPLAB ML.
2	
3	One row per PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW (~240 Hz). Each row carries the five raw
4	ADC values plus a set of binary labels whose meaning depends on `labels`:
5	
6	- `labels="detector"` (default, back-compat): five per-fret labels drawn from
7	  the most-recent PERF_REC_DETECTOR.pressed_mask, broadcast forward by
8	  frame_epoch (~4 fretboard samples per cv frame). Columns:
9	      timestamp,ph_green,...,ph_orange,
10	      label_green,label_red,label_yellow,label_blue,label_orange
11	- `labels="actuator"` (edge-ai distillation target): six labels drawn from the
12	  most-recent PERF_REC_ACTUATOR.intended_mask — five frets verbatim plus one
13	  collapsed strum bit (logical OR of strum-down and strum-up, since alternating
14	  direction is a human ergonomic constraint the controller doesn't enforce).
15	  Columns:
16	      timestamp,ph_green,...,ph_orange,
17	      fret_green,fret_red,fret_yellow,fret_blue,fret_orange,strum
18	
19	The collapse is a property of *this* exporter mode, not the raw capture:
20	PERF_REC_ACTUATOR keeps both strum bits as marvin emitted them, so a future
21	direction-aware corpus can preserve them. See tools/edge-ai/docs/training.md §2.
22	
23	`timestamp` is decimal seconds since the first emitted row's ts_counter.
24	
25	Edge cases:
26	- FretboardRaw records before the first label-source record (Detector or
27	  Actuator, depending on mode) are emitted with all labels = 0 by default;
28	  pass strict=True to drop them instead.
29	- Capture missing the SESSION record raises ExportError (no timer_freq_hz
30	  → no way to convert ts_counter to seconds).
31	"""
32	
33	from __future__ import annotations
34	
35	import csv
36	from dataclasses import dataclass
37	from pathlib import Path
38	
39	from ..capture import open_capture
40	from ..decode import decode_record
41	from ..framing import FrameStats, iter_frames
42	from ..records import Actuator, Detector, FretboardRaw, Session
43	from ..transport import FileSource
44	
45	
46	_HEADER_DETECTOR = (
47	    "timestamp",
48	    "ph_green", "ph_red", "ph_yellow", "ph_blue", "ph_orange",
49	    "label_green", "label_red", "label_yellow", "label_blue", "label_orange",
50	)
51	
52	_HEADER_ACTUATOR = (
53	    "timestamp",
54	    "ph_green", "ph_red", "ph_yellow", "ph_blue", "ph_orange",
55	    "fret_green", "fret_red", "fret_yellow", "fret_blue", "fret_orange",
56	    "strum",
57	)
58	
59	LABEL_MODES = ("detector", "actuator")
60	
61	
62	class ExportError(Exception):
63	    """Raised when a capture can't be exported (missing SESSION etc)."""
64	
65	
66	def _collapse_strum(intended_mask: int) -> int:
67	    """Collapse the 7-bit wire byte's two strum bits into one.
68	
69	    Bit 5 is strum-down, bit 6 is strum-up. The edge-ai model only learns
70	    *when* to strum, not direction, so the two collapse to a single bit.
71	    """
72	    return ((intended_mask >> 5) | (intended_mask >> 6)) & 1
73	
74	
75	@dataclass(frozen=True)
76	class ExportStats:
77	    n_rows: int
78	    n_skipped_unlabeled: int
79	    n_detector_records: int
80	    n_fretboard_records: int
81	    t_start_s: float
82	    t_end_s: float
83	    timer_freq_hz: int
84	    labels: str = "detector"
85	    n_actuator_records: int = 0
86	    # Rising-edge count of the collapsed strum bit (actuator mode only): the
87	    # number of distinct strums in the corpus, for sanity against the song.
88	    n_strum_events: int = 0
89	
90	    @property
91	    def duration_s(self) -> float:
92	        return self.t_end_s - self.t_start_s
93	
94	
95	def export_sensiml_csv(
96	    capture_path: str | Path,
97	    out_path: str | Path,
98	    *,
99	    labels: str = "detector",
100	    strict: bool = False,
101	) -> ExportStats:
102	    """Read `capture_path`, write SensiML-format CSV to `out_path`.
103	
104	    `labels` selects the label source: "detector" (per-fret pressed_mask,
105	    default, back-compat) or "actuator" (5 frets + collapsed strum from
106	    Actuator.intended_mask — the edge-ai distillation target).
107	
108	    `strict=True` drops FretboardRaw rows that arrive before the first
109	    label-source record (so every emitted row has a real label). Default is
110	    to emit them with all labels = 0 — useful when the capture starts before
111	    the label source has produced its first record.
112	    """
113	    if labels not in LABEL_MODES:
114	        raise ExportError(
115	            f"unknown labels mode {labels!r}; expected one of {LABEL_MODES}"
116	        )
117	
118	    capture = open_capture(capture_path)
119	
120	    session: Session | None = None
121	    last_detector: Detector | None = None
122	    last_actuator: Actuator | None = None
123	    n_skipped_unlabeled = 0
124	    n_detector_records = 0
125	    n_actuator_records = 0
126	    n_fretboard_records = 0
127	    n_rows = 0
128	    n_strum_events = 0
129	    prev_strum = 0
130	    t_baseline: int | None = None  # ts_counter of the first emitted row
131	    t_end_s = 0.0
132	
133	    header = _HEADER_ACTUATOR if labels == "actuator" else _HEADER_DETECTOR
134	
135	    out_path = Path(out_path)
136	    with FileSource(capture.bin_path) as src, out_path.open("w", newline="") as fh:
137	        writer = csv.writer(fh)
138	        writer.writerow(header)
139	        stats = FrameStats()
140	
141	        for frame in iter_frames(src, stats):
142	            try:
143	                rec = decode_record(frame.payload)
144	            except Exception:
145	                continue
146	
147	            if isinstance(rec, Session) and session is None:
148	                session = rec
149	                continue
150	
151	            if isinstance(rec, Detector):
152	                last_detector = rec
153	                n_detector_records += 1
154	                continue
155	
156	            if isinstance(rec, Actuator):
157	                last_actuator = rec
158	                n_actuator_records += 1
159	                continue
160	
161	            if isinstance(rec, FretboardRaw):
162	                n_fretboard_records += 1
163	                if session is None:
164	                    # No timer_freq_hz yet → can't write a real timestamp.
165	                    # Defer rejection to after the loop so we still tally
166	                    # how many records were skipped for diagnostics.
167	                    n_skipped_unlabeled += 1
168	                    continue
169	
170	                have_label = (
171	                    last_actuator is not None
172	                    if labels == "actuator"
173	                    else last_detector is not None
174	                )
175	                if not have_label and strict:
176	                    n_skipped_unlabeled += 1
177	                    continue
178	
179	                if t_baseline is None:
180	                    t_baseline = rec.hdr.ts_counter
181	                t_s = (rec.hdr.ts_counter - t_baseline) / float(
182	                    session.timer_freq_hz
183	                )
184	                t_end_s = t_s
185	
186	                adc = (
187	                    rec.adc[0], rec.adc[1], rec.adc[2], rec.adc[3], rec.adc[4],
188	                )
189	                if labels == "actuator":
190	                    mask = last_actuator.intended_mask if last_actuator else 0
191	                    strum = _collapse_strum(mask)
192	                    if strum and not prev_strum:
193	                        n_strum_events += 1
194	                    prev_strum = strum
195	                    row = [
196	                        f"{t_s:.6f}", *adc,
197	                        (mask >> 0) & 1,
198	                        (mask >> 1) & 1,
199	                        (mask >> 2) & 1,
200	                        (mask >> 3) & 1,
201	                        (mask >> 4) & 1,
202	                        strum,
203	                    ]
204	                else:
205	                    pressed = last_detector.pressed_mask if last_detector else 0
206	                    row = [
207	                        f"{t_s:.6f}", *adc,
208	                        (pressed >> 0) & 1,
209	                        (pressed >> 1) & 1,
210	                        (pressed >> 2) & 1,
211	                        (pressed >> 3) & 1,
212	                        (pressed >> 4) & 1,
213	                    ]
214	                writer.writerow(row)
215	                n_rows += 1
216	
217	    if session is None:
218	        # Tear out the partial file before raising — exporting half a file
219	        # with no header is more confusing than an absent file.
220	        try:
221	            out_path.unlink()
222	        except FileNotFoundError:
223	            pass
224	        raise ExportError(
225	            f"capture {capture.path} has no SESSION record — cannot derive "
226	            "timer_freq_hz to compute timestamps"
227	        )
228	
229	    return ExportStats(
230	        n_rows=n_rows,
231	        n_skipped_unlabeled=n_skipped_unlabeled,
232	        n_detector_records=n_detector_records,
233	        n_fretboard_records=n_fretboard_records,
234	        t_start_s=0.0,
235	        t_end_s=t_end_s,
236	        timer_freq_hz=session.timer_freq_hz,
237	        labels=labels,
238	        n_actuator_records=n_actuator_records,
239	        n_strum_events=n_strum_events,
240	    )
241

167	        RecordType.ACTUATOR, frame_epoch=frame_epoch, ts_counter=ts_counter
168	    ) + body
169	
170	
171	def build_task_highwater_payload(*, task_id: int, words: int) -> bytes:
172	    body = TaskHighwater._BODY.pack(task_id, b"\x00\x00\x00", words)
173	    return build_header(RecordType.TASK_HIGHWATER) + body
174	
175	
176	def build_task_runtime_payload(
177	    *,
178	    task_id: int,
179	    state: int,
180	    priority: int,
181	    run_time_counter: int = 0,
182	    ts_counter: int = 0,
183	) -> bytes:
184	    body = TaskRuntime._BODY.pack(task_id, state, priority, 0, run_time_counter, 0)
185	    return build_header(RecordType.TASK_RUNTIME, ts_counter=ts_counter) + body
186	
187	
188	def build_strip_payload(
189	    *,
190	    frame_epoch: int = 1,
191	    kind: int = int(StripKind.SENSING),
192	    x: int = 240,
193	    y: int = 295,
194	    w: int = 4,
195	    h: int = 2,
196	    fill: int = 0x55,
197	) -> bytes:
198	    body = _STRIP_BODY.pack(x, y, w, h, kind, b"\x00\x00\x00")
199	    bgr = bytes((fill,) * (w * h * STRIP_BPP))
200	    return build_header(RecordType.STRIP, frame_epoch=frame_epoch) + body + bgr
201	
202	
203	# ─── Frame wrapper (SOF + LEN + payload + FCS) ───────────────────────────────
204	
205	
206	def wrap_frame(payload: bytes, *, corrupt_fcs: bool = False) -> bytes:
207	    length = len(payload)
208	    length_bytes = struct.pack("<H", length)
209	    fcs = fletcher16(length_bytes + payload)
210	    if corrupt_fcs:
211	        fcs ^= 0xFFFF
212	    return SOF_BYTES + length_bytes + payload + struct.pack("<H", fcs)
213
```

44	def _build_session_first(ts_counter: int = 0) -> bytes:
45	    """SESSION record body builder doesn't expose ts_counter; patch it in."""
46	    import struct
47	    from marvin_perf.records import PERF_LOG_HDR_MAGIC, RecordType, Session
48	
49	    hdr = struct.pack(
50	        "<HBBIQ", PERF_LOG_HDR_MAGIC, int(RecordType.SESSION), 0, 0, ts_counter
51	    )
52	    body = Session._BODY.pack(_TIMER_HZ, 3, 0, 0, 0)
53	    return hdr + body

56	def _make_capture(tmp_path: Path) -> Path:
57	    """A small synthetic capture covering the join paths.

60	      SESSION                                                ts=0
61	      DETECTOR  epoch=1  pressed=0b00000  (no presses)       ts=10_000
62	      FRETBOARD_RAW × 4  epoch=1  adc=(100,200,...)          ts=10_000 + 0..3 ticks
63	      DETECTOR  epoch=2  pressed=0b00001  (green pressed)    ts=10_000 + 1 frame
64	      FRETBOARD_RAW × 4  epoch=2  adc=(50,...)               ts=...
65	      DETECTOR  epoch=3  pressed=0b00101  (green+yellow)     ts=...
66	      FRETBOARD_RAW × 4  epoch=3  adc=(40,...)               ts=...
67	
68	    First detector record arrives BEFORE the first fretboard record so the
69	    "skipped pre-detector" path is covered by a separate test.

Without this patch the host CDC driver accepts the IAD via the TPL match (TPL ignores subclass/protocol) but rejects the comm interface inside `F_USB_HOST_CDC_InterfaceAssign`, the interrupt pipe never opens, the CDC instance flips to `STATE_ERROR`, and the app-level attach handler never fires. Patch: extend each check to `(... == AT_V250 || ... == NO_CLASS_SPECIFIC)`. Two one-line OR additions. Re-apply after every USB-host MCC regen.

Root cause: `PerfLog_EmitDetector` was defined in [`perf_log.c:453`](../default/src/perf_log/perf_log.c#L453) and declared in [`perf_log.h:31`](../default/src/perf_log/perf_log.h#L31) but **never actually called from anywhere**. cv_marvin_v1's `detect_frame` was building a `detector_state_t`, posting it to the detector bus (which is why the actuator/timing pipeline runs and the game plays correctly), but skipping the perf-log mirror of the same per-frame decision.
Fix: add the call at the bottom of [`cv_marvin_v1.c:detect_frame`](../default/src/detector/cv_marvin_v1.c) right after the bus push. Build `hold_dist[]` / `edge_dist[]` / `pressed_mask` / `edge_active_mask` from the same struct fields the bus message carried (`state.fret[i].raw_value`, `state.fret[i].confidence`, `s_pressed[i]`, `s_edge_active[i]`). The perf-log struct's hold/edge values already share the 0..65535 scaling with `detector_state_t.{raw_value, confidence}` per the schema comment, so no rescaling needed.
First real export-ml run on hardware tripped over a missing `SESSION` record in the bin: the firmware emits SESSION exactly once per sink-attach edge, but the web-mode recorder doesn't start mirroring framed bytes to disk until the user clicks Record — usually well after attach. By then the SESSION has been received and consumed by the reader thread, but it's never written to the recording's bin, so the offline exporter can't recover `timer_freq_hz`.
Fix in [`tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/web/live.py`](../../../tools/marvin-perf/marvin_perf/web/live.py): cache the framed bytes of each "prepend-worthy" record type into a `prepend_framed: dict[str, bytes]`. On `record_start`, write the cached bytes to the new bin in declared order before letting the live mirror take over. The two types covered today:
- **DETECTOR_CONFIG** — re-emits at ~1 Hz from cv_marvin_v1 ([cv_marvin_v1.c:374](../default/src/detector/cv_marvin_v1.c#L374)) but a sub-second capture might end before the next heartbeat. Carries cv sample coords + thresholds + colour weights — needed by the offline review UI to render STRIP overlays from frame 0 and useful for auditability of the detector configuration that produced the labels.
Other 1 Hz heartbeats (`DROP`, `TASK_HIGHWATER`, `TASK_RUNTIME`) are cumulative counters; the second sample (1 second in) gives the same info, no prepend needed. Per-event records (`STAMP`, `DETECTOR`, `TIMING`, `STRIP`, `ACTUATOR`, `FRETBOARD_RAW`) are high-rate and self-contained. New types added in the future just need an entry in `_PREPEND_TYPES`.
The headless `marvin-perf record` path was never affected: opening the serial port toggles DTR, which fires the firmware-side SESSION emit, which lands in the very first frames of the bin.
Step 2 of the Edge-AI training-dataset workstream. Capture pipeline was already wiring `PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW` (240 Hz) and `PERF_REC_DETECTOR` (60 Hz) through marvin-perf's recording sink; this session adds the offline export that turns one of those captures into a labelled CSV ready for [MPLAB Machine Learning Development Suite](https://www.microchip.com/en-us/tools-resources/develop/mplab-machine-learning-development-suite) / SensiML Data Capture Lab.

```text
1	"""Wire-frame parser for the perf-log USB CDC stream.
2	
3	Wire layout (mirrors firmware perf_log_sink_cdc.c):
4	
5	    SOF(4)  | LEN(u16 LE) | PAYLOAD(LEN bytes) | FCS(u16 LE)
6	
7	FCS is Fletcher-16 (mod 255, init 0xFFFF) computed over `LEN || PAYLOAD`
8	(NOT including SOF). USB hardware already CRCs the wire; the framing
9	checksum is just for resync alignment + firmware-bug detection.
10	
11	This module is purely byte-level. It does not understand record types — that's
12	decode.py's job. It exists to (a) resync after mid-stream join or byte loss,
13	(b) reject corrupt frames, and (c) yield validated payloads upward.
14	"""
15	
16	from __future__ import annotations
17	
18	from collections.abc import Iterable, Iterator
19	from dataclasses import dataclass
20	
21	from .records import MAX_RECORD_BYTES, SOF_BYTES
22	
23	
24	# ─── Fletcher-16 (mod 255, init 0xFFFF) ──────────────────────────────────────
25	
26	
27	def fletcher16(data: bytes | memoryview, init: int = 0xFFFF) -> int:
28	    """Fletcher-16 with mod 255. Mirrors firmware perf_log_sink_cdc.c.
29	
30	    Detection: single-byte changes, adjacent swaps, most non-adjacent swaps.
31	    Strong enough for framing-layer alignment + firmware-bug detection on
32	    top of USB's wire-level CRC. ~3× cheaper than CRC-16 in C and Python.
33	    """
34	    s1 = init & 0xFF
35	    s2 = (init >> 8) & 0xFF
36	    for b in data:
37	        s1 = (s1 + b) % 255
38	        s2 = (s2 + s1) % 255
39	    return (s2 << 8) | s1
40	
41	
42	def frame_encode(payload: bytes) -> bytes:
43	    """SOF + LEN(u16LE) + payload + Fletcher-16(u16LE).
44	
45	    Mirror of the device-side framer; FCS covers LEN || PAYLOAD (not SOF).
46	    """
47	    length = len(payload)
48	    if length > 0xFFFF:
49	        raise ValueError(f"payload too large: {length} bytes")
50	    len_bytes = bytes((length & 0xFF, (length >> 8) & 0xFF))
51	    fcs = fletcher16(len_bytes + payload)
52	    fcs_bytes = bytes((fcs & 0xFF, (fcs >> 8) & 0xFF))
53	    return SOF_BYTES + len_bytes + payload + fcs_bytes
54	
55	
56	# ─── Frame iterator ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
57	
58	
59	@dataclass(frozen=True)
60	class FrameBytes:
61	    """A successfully-parsed wire frame's payload + provenance."""
62	
63	    payload: bytes
64	    bytes_skipped_before: int  # diagnostic: bytes dropped resyncing to this frame
65	    framed: bytes = b""        # full SOF+LEN+payload+CRC for re-emission to disk
66	
67	
68	class FrameError(Exception):
69	    """Wire-level frame error (FCS mismatch, length out of range)."""
70	
71	
72	class FrameStats:
73	    """Mutable counters surfaced by `iter_frames` for the CLI."""
74	
75	    def __init__(self) -> None:
76	        self.frames_ok: int = 0
77	        self.bytes_resync_dropped: int = 0
78	        self.fcs_mismatches: int = 0
79	        self.bad_lengths: int = 0
80	
81	
82	def iter_frames(
83	    chunks: Iterable[bytes],
84	    stats: FrameStats | None = None,
85	) -> Iterator[FrameBytes]:
86	    """Consume an iterable of byte chunks, yield validated frame payloads.
87	
88	    The iterator handles arbitrary chunk boundaries (a frame may straddle as
89	    many chunks as it likes), resyncs on the 4-byte SOF after byte loss, and
90	    drops frames whose FCS does not match. Counters are accumulated into
91	    `stats` if supplied.
92	    """
93	    if stats is None:
94	        stats = FrameStats()
95	
96	    buf = bytearray()
97	    skipped_since_last_ok = 0
98	
99	    for chunk in chunks:
100	        if not chunk:
101	            continue
102	        buf.extend(chunk)
103	
104	        while True:
105	            sof_idx = buf.find(SOF_BYTES)
106	            if sof_idx < 0:
107	                # No SOF in buffer. Drop everything but the last 3 bytes (a
108	                # SOF could still be straddling the boundary).
109	                if len(buf) > 3:
110	                    skipped_since_last_ok += len(buf) - 3
111	                    stats.bytes_resync_dropped += len(buf) - 3
112	                    del buf[: len(buf) - 3]
113	                break
114	
115	            if sof_idx > 0:
116	                skipped_since_last_ok += sof_idx
117	                stats.bytes_resync_dropped += sof_idx
118	                del buf[:sof_idx]
119	
120	            # buf now starts with SOF. Need 4 (SOF) + 2 (LEN) before we can
121	            # bound the frame.
122	            if len(buf) < 6:
123	                break
124	
125	            length = buf[4] | (buf[5] << 8)
126	
127	            # Sanity-bound the length. A bogus LEN (e.g. mid-payload bytes
128	            # that happened to align with SOF) will trip this; treat the SOF
129	            # as a false positive and step past it.
130	            if length < 16 or length > MAX_RECORD_BYTES:
131	                stats.bad_lengths += 1
132	                skipped_since_last_ok += 1
133	                stats.bytes_resync_dropped += 1
134	                del buf[0]
135	                continue
136	
137	            total = 6 + length + 2
138	            if len(buf) < total:
139	                break
140	
141	            payload = bytes(buf[6 : 6 + length])
142	            fcs_observed = buf[6 + length] | (buf[6 + length + 1] << 8)
143	            fcs_expected = fletcher16(buf[4 : 6 + length])
144	
145	            if fcs_observed != fcs_expected:
146	                # Bad FCS. Likely a false-positive SOF in the middle of an
147	                # earlier frame; step past one byte and rescan.
148	                stats.fcs_mismatches += 1
149	                skipped_since_last_ok += 1
150	                stats.bytes_resync_dropped += 1

```text
| **fretboard board** (PIC32CM6408PL10048) | Sensor + actuator MCU | USB CDC host (marvin is USB host to fretboard's on-board EDBG composite, VID=0x03EB PID=0x2175; CDC ACM bridged to SERCOM1 PB00/PB01 at 115 200 Bd). |
- **Fretboard → marvin:** raw ADC stream (5 channels × 16-bit) at 240 Hz, in a 12-byte start/end-bracketed frame. Marvin's `fretboard_link` issues a continuously-rearming `USB_HOST_CDC_Read` and a sibling `fretboard_rx_task` parses each valid frame and republishes it as a `PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW` perf-log record (default-disabled, host enables via `PERF_CMD_SET_TYPE_MASK`). This is the on-board capture path until the SD-card recorder lands; it's also the substrate for the future `adc_fretboard` detector (§4.2).
- **`adc_raw.bin`** — fretboard 12-byte frames at 240 Hz with `frame_epoch` annotation = ~2.9 KB/s. Modest. Until the SD recorder lands, the same data is available live as `PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW` records (28 B framed) in any marvin-perf capture (default-disabled; enable with `set-mask`).
```

2	
3	Operates on a `list[Record]` (session sizes are small enough at v0 — state-only
4	~9 KB/s × minutes is a few MB; even adding patches we stay under tens of MB).
5	Three deliverables:
6	
7	1. Latency attribution — per-frame stage transitions in microseconds with
8	   p50/p95/p99/max histograms.
9	2. Drop accounting — deltas across the cumulative DROP record stream.
10	3. Stack high-water trend — per-task HWM over session time.
11	
12	Plus always-on sanity checks:
13	- SESSION schema_version match (hard fail)
14	- frame_epoch monotonicity (warning)
15	- Inter-VIDEO_PUBLISH delta (warning if outside 16.67 ms ± 2 ms at 60 Hz)
16	"""
17	
18	from __future__ import annotations
19	
20	from collections import defaultdict
21	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
22	from typing import Iterable
23	
24	from .records import (
25	    Drop,

39	
40	class SchemaVersionMismatch(Exception):
41	    """Raised when SESSION.schema_version does not match host expectation."""
42

46	    kind: str
47	    message: str

50	# ─── Latency attribution ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
51	
52	# Stage transitions the firmware is wired to emit (per perf_log_records.h:39-48
53	# and the journal's producer-wiring plan). Only adjacent pairs in a single
54	# frame's pipeline make sense.
55	STAGE_PAIRS: tuple[tuple[Stage, Stage], ...] = (
56	    (Stage.ISC_IRQ, Stage.VIDEO_PUBLISH),
57	    (Stage.VIDEO_PUBLISH, Stage.CV_START),
58	    (Stage.CV_START, Stage.CV_END),
59	    (Stage.CV_END, Stage.TP_TICK),
60	    (Stage.TP_TICK, Stage.FBL_SEND),
61	    (Stage.FBL_SEND, Stage.CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE),
62	)
63	
64	
65	@dataclass
66	class LatencyHist:
67	    pair: tuple[Stage, Stage]
68	    samples_us: list[float] = field(default_factory=list)
69	
70	    @property
71	    def n(self) -> int:
72	        return len(self.samples_us)
73	
74	    def percentile(self, p: float) -> float:
75	        if not self.samples_us:
76	            return float("nan")
77	        ordered = sorted(self.samples_us)
78	        # nearest-rank percentile, clamped to last index
79	        rank = max(0, min(len(ordered) - 1, int(p * len(ordered))))
80	        return ordered[rank]
81	
82	    @property
83	    def p50(self) -> float: return self.percentile(0.50)
84	    @property
85	    def p95(self) -> float: return self.percentile(0.95)
86	    @property
87	    def p99(self) -> float: return self.percentile(0.99)
88	    @property
89	    def max(self) -> float:
90	        return max(self.samples_us) if self.samples_us else float("nan")
91	
92	
93	def compute_latencies(
94	    records: Iterable[Record],
95	    timer_freq_hz: int,
96	) -> list[LatencyHist]:
97	    """Group Stamp records by frame_epoch, derive per-pair deltas in µs."""
98	    by_epoch: dict[int, dict[int, int]] = defaultdict(dict)
99	    for rec in records:
100	        if not isinstance(rec, Stamp):
101	            continue
102	        # Last write wins on duplicate stage in a single epoch — that's a
103	        # producer bug worth surfacing later, but for v0 we simply take latest.
104	        by_epoch[rec.hdr.frame_epoch][rec.stage_id] = rec.hdr.ts_counter
105	
106	    hists = [LatencyHist(pair=p) for p in STAGE_PAIRS]
107	    if timer_freq_hz <= 0:
108	        return hists
109	
110	    us_per_tick = 1_000_000.0 / float(timer_freq_hz)
111	    for stages in by_epoch.values():
112	        for hist in hists:
113	            a, b = hist.pair
114	            t_a = stages.get(int(a))
115	            t_b = stages.get(int(b))
116	            if t_a is None or t_b is None:
117	                continue
118	            delta = t_b - t_a
119	            if delta < 0:
120	                continue  # 64-bit counter is monotonic; defensive only
121	            hist.samples_us.append(delta * us_per_tick)
122	    return hists
123

128	@dataclass
129	class DropSummary:
130	    # Cumulative since firmware boot — `dropped_sink` is bytes, the others
131	    # are records (the firmware-side counter unit mismatch lives in
132	    # perf_log_sink_cdc.c:223 / perf_log.c:218,278).
133	    final_state: int = 0
134	    final_strip: int = 0
135	    final_sink_bytes: int = 0
136	    # Deltas from the first DROP record observed in this capture, which is
137	    # what users actually want when they attach mid-session: the pre-attach
138	    # cumulative is noise.
139	    since_session_state: int = 0
140	    since_session_strip: int = 0
141	    since_session_sink_bytes: int = 0
142	    n_drop_records: int = 0
143	    max_state_delta: int = 0
144	    max_strip_delta: int = 0
145	    max_sink_bytes_delta: int = 0
146	
147	
148	def compute_drops(records: Iterable[Record]) -> DropSummary:
149	    """Walk DROP records (cumulative since boot) and surface session-relative deltas."""
150	    summary = DropSummary()
151	    baseline: Drop | None = None
152	    prev: Drop | None = None
153	    for rec in records:
154	        if not isinstance(rec, Drop):
155	            continue
156	        summary.n_drop_records += 1
157	        if baseline is None:
158	            baseline = rec
159	        if prev is not None:
160	            summary.max_state_delta = max(
161	                summary.max_state_delta, rec.dropped_state - prev.dropped_state
162	            )
163	            summary.max_strip_delta = max(
164	                summary.max_strip_delta, rec.dropped_strip - prev.dropped_strip
165	            )
166	            summary.max_sink_bytes_delta = max(
167	                summary.max_sink_bytes_delta, rec.dropped_sink - prev.dropped_sink
168	            )
169	        summary.final_state = rec.dropped_state
170	        summary.final_strip = rec.dropped_strip
171	        summary.final_sink_bytes = rec.dropped_sink
172	        prev = rec
173	    if baseline is not None:
174	        summary.since_session_state = summary.final_state - baseline.dropped_state
175	        summary.since_session_strip = summary.final_strip - baseline.dropped_strip
176	        summary.since_session_sink_bytes = (
177	            summary.final_sink_bytes - baseline.dropped_sink
178	        )
179	    return summary

187	    task_id: int
188	    samples: list[tuple[int, int]] = field(default_factory=list)  # (ts_counter, words)
189	
190	    @property
191	    def task_name(self) -> str:
192	        try:
193	            return TaskId(self.task_id).name
194	        except ValueError:
195	            return f"task_{self.task_id}"
196

199	        return min((w for _, w in self.samples), default=0)
200

202	def compute_hwm(records: Iterable[Record]) -> dict[int, HwmSeries]:
203	    out: dict[int, HwmSeries] = {}
204	    for rec in records:
205	        if not isinstance(rec, TaskHighwater):
206	            continue
207	        s = out.setdefault(rec.task_id, HwmSeries(task_id=rec.task_id))
208	        s.samples.append((rec.hdr.ts_counter, rec.words))
209	    return out

211	
212	# ─── CPU% snapshot ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
213	
214	# Firmware emits TASK_RUNTIME records for every registered slot once per second
215	# from PerfDrain (perf_log.c:225) — including PERF_TASK_IDLE and PERF_TASK_OTHER
216	# (Σ all − Σ registered). Per-task CPU% over the most recent 1 s window is
217	# Δrun_time_counter[task] / Σ Δrun_time_counter[*]; uint32 wraps at 266 MHz
218	# every ~16 s of accumulated busy time per task, so a wrap inside a 1 s window
219	# is impossible — but we mask anyway so a stale reference doesn't blow up.
220	
221	
222	@dataclass
223	class CpuSnapshot:
224	    task_id: int
225	    run_time_delta: int          # uint32-wrap-safe Δrun_time_counter
226	    window_ticks: int            # ts_counter delta between the two samples
227	    cpu_pct: float               # 0..100, normalized against Σ across all tasks
228	
229	
230	def _u32_delta(a: int, b: int) -> int:
231	    """Wrap-safe (b - a) for uint32 cumulative counters."""
232	    return (b - a) & 0xFFFFFFFF
233	
234	
235	def compute_cpu_snapshot(
236	    records: Iterable[Record],
237	) -> dict[int, CpuSnapshot]:
238	    """Last-window CPU% per task, computed from the two most recent
239	    TASK_RUNTIME records per task. Returns {} until each task has at least
240	    two samples.
241	
242	    The percentage normalizes against the sum of deltas across every task
243	    that emitted in the window, including IDLE (so absolute %busy = 100 −
244	    cpu_pct[IDLE]) and OTHER (Σ all − Σ registered, a firmware-side
245	    closure of un-named work). Tasks present only as a single sample
246	    contribute 0 and don't appear in the result.
247	    """
248	    last_two: dict[int, list[TaskRuntime]] = defaultdict(list)
249	    for rec in records:
250	        if not isinstance(rec, TaskRuntime):
251	            continue
252	        bucket = last_two[rec.task_id]
253	        bucket.append(rec)
254	        # Keep only the two most recent.
255	        if len(bucket) > 2:
256	            del bucket[0]
257	
258	    deltas: dict[int, tuple[int, int]] = {}  # task_id → (run_delta, ts_delta)
259	    for tid, bucket in last_two.items():
260	        if len(bucket) < 2:
261	            continue
262	        a, b = bucket[0], bucket[1]
263	        deltas[tid] = (
264	            _u32_delta(a.run_time_counter, b.run_time_counter),
265	            b.hdr.ts_counter - a.hdr.ts_counter,
266	        )
267	
268	    total = sum(d for d, _ in deltas.values())
269	    out: dict[int, CpuSnapshot] = {}
270	    if total <= 0:
271	        return out
272	    for tid, (run_delta, ts_delta) in deltas.items():
273	        out[tid] = CpuSnapshot(
274	            task_id=tid,
275	            run_time_delta=run_delta,
276	            window_ticks=ts_delta,
277	            cpu_pct=100.0 * run_delta / total,
278	        )
279	    return out
280

```text
1	"""Load actuator-labelled SensiML CSVs and build causal training windows.
2	
3	The CSV is produced by `marvin-perf export-ml --labels=actuator`:
4	
5	    timestamp,
6	    ph_green,ph_red,ph_yellow,ph_blue,ph_orange,
7	    fret_green,fret_red,fret_yellow,fret_blue,fret_orange,
8	    strum
9	
10	Each row is one true 240 Hz fretboard sample. Windows are sliced **by row
11	index**, never by the `timestamp` column — timestamps are bursty (stamped at
12	marvin's USB-CDC RX time, not the sample instant; see the edge-ai journal).
13	
14	CSV parsing, the window-index logic, and label/feature extraction are
15	stdlib-only. `build_arrays` materialises numpy tensors and imports numpy
16	lazily so the rest of the module loads without it.
17	"""
18	
19	from __future__ import annotations
20	
21	import csv
22	from dataclasses import dataclass
23	from pathlib import Path
24	
25	from . import FRET_COUNT, N_LABELS
26	
27	EXPECTED_HEADER = [
28	    "timestamp",
29	    "ph_green", "ph_red", "ph_yellow", "ph_blue", "ph_orange",
30	    "fret_green", "fret_red", "fret_yellow", "fret_blue", "fret_orange",
31	    "strum",
32	]
33	
34	
35	class DataError(Exception):
36	    """Raised on a malformed or wrong-schema CSV."""
37	
38	
39	@dataclass(frozen=True)
40	class Capture:
41	    """One loaded capture. `adc[i]` is a 5-tuple, `labels[i]` a 6-tuple."""
42	
43	    name: str
44	    timestamps: list[float]
45	    adc: list[tuple[int, ...]]
46	    labels: list[tuple[int, ...]]
47	
48	    def __len__(self) -> int:
49	        return len(self.adc)
50	
51	    @property
52	    def strum_fraction(self) -> float:
53	        if not self.labels:
54	            return 0.0
55	        return sum(row[5] for row in self.labels) / len(self.labels)
56	
57	    @property
58	    def n_strum_events(self) -> int:
59	        prev = 0
60	        n = 0
61	        for row in self.labels:
62	            if row[5] and not prev:
63	                n += 1
64	            prev = row[5]
65	        return n
66	
67	
68	def load_capture(path: str | Path) -> Capture:
69	    """Read one actuator-labelled CSV into a Capture (stdlib only)."""
70	    path = Path(path)
71	    with path.open(newline="") as fh:
72	        reader = csv.reader(fh)
73	        try:
74	            header = next(reader)
75	        except StopIteration:
76	            raise DataError(f"{path}: empty file")
77	        if header != EXPECTED_HEADER:
78	            raise DataError(
79	                f"{path}: header is not the actuator schema.\n"
80	                f"  expected: {EXPECTED_HEADER}\n"
81	                f"  got:      {header}\n"
82	                "Export with `marvin-perf export-ml --labels=actuator`."
83	            )
84	        timestamps: list[float] = []
85	        adc: list[tuple[int, ...]] = []
86	        labels: list[tuple[int, ...]] = []
87	        for lineno, row in enumerate(reader, start=2):
88	            if len(row) != len(EXPECTED_HEADER):
89	                raise DataError(f"{path}:{lineno}: expected 12 fields, got {len(row)}")
90	            timestamps.append(float(row[0]))
91	            adc.append(tuple(int(row[1 + c]) for c in range(FRET_COUNT)))
92	            labels.append(tuple(int(row[6 + b]) for b in range(N_LABELS)))
93	    return Capture(name=path.stem, timestamps=timestamps, adc=adc, labels=labels)
94	
95	
96	def causal_window_indices(n_rows: int, window: int) -> list[tuple[int, int, int]]:
97	    """Causal "now-cast" windows over a single capture's rows.
98	
99	    Returns `(start, end, label_row)` triples where rows `[start, end)` are the
100	    `window` feature samples (end is exclusive) and the label is taken at
101	    `label_row = end - 1` — i.e. the window ends *at* the row being predicted,
102	    so only past+present samples feed the prediction. Rows before the first
103	    full window have insufficient history and are skipped.
104	    """
105	    if window < 1:
106	        raise ValueError("window must be >= 1")
107	    return [(i - window + 1, i + 1, i) for i in range(window - 1, n_rows)]
108	
109	
110	def compute_norm_stats(captures: list[Capture]):
111	    """Per-channel (mean, std) over all rows, for input standardisation.
112	
113	    Standardising the narrow ADC band (idle ≈ 3900, dips ≈ 1000) is what makes
114	    the net trainable; raw /4095 leaves inputs clustered near 0.95 and starves
115	    gradients. The affine folds into the int8 input quantisation at deploy, so
116	    this stays deploy-compatible. Returns numpy arrays (mean[5], std[5]).
117	    """
118	    import numpy as np
119	
120	    rows = np.concatenate(
121	        [np.asarray(c.adc, dtype=np.float32) for c in captures if len(c) > 0], axis=0
122	    )
123	    mean = rows.mean(axis=0)
124	    std = rows.std(axis=0)
125	    std[std < 1e-6] = 1.0
126	    return mean, std
127	
128	
129	def _dilate_strum(strum, k: int):
130	    """Widen each strum positive by ±k samples (training labels only)."""
131	    import numpy as np
132	
133	    out = strum.copy()
134	    for off in range(1, k + 1):
135	        out[off:] = np.maximum(out[off:], strum[:-off])
136	        out[:-off] = np.maximum(out[:-off], strum[off:])
137	    return out
138	
139	
140	def build_arrays(
141	    captures: list[Capture],
142	    window: int,
143	    *,
144	    stats=None,
145	    strum_dilate: int = 0,
146	):
147	    """Materialise (X, Y, stats) for all captures, windowed per capture.
148	
149	    X: float32 (n_windows, FRET_COUNT, window) — channels-first for Conv1d,
150	       per-channel standardised by `stats` (computed from `captures` if None).
151	    Y: float32 (n_windows, N_LABELS) — the 6 label bits at each window's
152	       label_row. With `strum_dilate>0` the strum label (bit 5) is widened by
153	       ±k samples so a near-miss isn't fully penalised — use for *training*
154	       only, never for eval.
155	
156	    Windows never cross capture boundaries (no song bleeds into another).
157	    """
158	    import numpy as np
159	
160	    if stats is None:
161	        stats = compute_norm_stats(captures)
162	    mean, std = stats
163	
164	    xs = []
165	    ys = []
166	    for cap in captures:
167	        if len(cap) < window:
168	            continue
169	        adc = (np.asarray(cap.adc, dtype=np.float32) - mean) / std  # (rows, 5)
170	        lab = np.asarray(cap.labels, dtype=np.float32)              # (rows, 6)
171	        if strum_dilate > 0:
172	            lab = lab.copy()
173	            lab[:, 5] = _dilate_strum(lab[:, 5], strum_dilate)
174	        idx = causal_window_indices(len(cap), window)
175	        for start, end, label_row in idx:
176	            xs.append(adc[start:end].T)        # (5, window)
177	            ys.append(lab[label_row])          # (6,)
178	    if not xs:
179	        raise DataError(
180	            f"no windows produced — every capture shorter than window={window}?"
181	        )
182	    return np.stack(xs).astype(np.float32), np.stack(ys).astype(np.float32), stats
183	
184	
185	def strum_pos_weight(captures: list[Capture]) -> float:
186	    """Inverse-frequency positive weight for the sparse strum bit: (neg/pos)."""
187	    pos = sum(row[5] for cap in captures for row in cap.labels)
188	    total = sum(len(cap) for cap in captures)
189	    neg = total - pos
190	    return (neg / pos) if pos else 1.0
191

        case PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW:   return (uint16_t)sizeof(perf_rec_fretboard_raw_t);
        default:                       return (uint16_t)sizeof(perf_hdr_t);
    }
}

/* Variable-length: queue slot is max-sized, but on the wire we send only
 * HDR + body + the actually-used pixel bytes. */
static uint16_t strip_record_size(const perf_rec_strip_t *r)
{
    uint32_t pix = (uint32_t)r->w * (uint32_t)r->h * PERF_STRIP_BPP;
    if (pix > PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES) { pix = PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES; }
    return (uint16_t)(PERF_STRIP_HDR_BYTES + pix);
}

/* ─── Drain task ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */

static void emit_session_record(void)
{
    perf_rec_session_t r;
    memset(&r, 0, sizeof(r));
    hdr_fill(&r.hdr, PERF_REC_SESSION, 0u, 0u);
```

## Decision log

| Date | Decision | Rationale |
